sequence.name: Thunderdome
sequence.text:
1
Thunderdome
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Thunderdomes are advanced workouts for those who have plateaued. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before attempting a Thunderdome.

For each stimulus in the section*, write or speak out each and every one of the following outputs, according to the stimulus type, without looking at the question stem or answer choices:

On an Argument, write or speak your own:

Weaken correct answer

Strengthen correct answer

Necessary assumption

Sufficient assumption

Method correct answer

Argument parts identifications

Parallel Skeleton

Parallel correct answer

Use your favorite topic as a consistent analogous base

This means all your Parallel correct answers can be about dogs or cars across all the questions in the section.

On a Debate, write or speak your own:

Controversy

Agreement

Loophole in both speakers

On a Paradox, write or speak your own:

Resolution

Inference

Contradiction

sequence.name: Party Tricking Jail
sequence.text:
4
Party Tricking Jail
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Party Tricking Jail is an advanced workout for those who want to push themselves to become true answer choice experts. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before entering Party Tricking Jail.

Party Trick every question in an LR or RC section*.

This means you will only read the question stem and answer choices on each question before you select an answer on that question.

Do not look at the stimulus or passage.

Camo the section immediately after completing it.

The Camo will display all the questions that are wrong plus an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Do not look at the stimulus when you Camo.

Party Trick the returned questions again. Doubt your answers on the questions Camo displays and try to correct your answer.

Get as close to -0 on the Camo as you can.

OPTIONAL: Do not exit Party Tricking Jail until you reach -5 or better pre-Camo.

You can customize this accuracy goal to your personal needs.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Scavenger Hunt
sequence.text:
5
Scavenger Hunt
Instructions

At the end of the week, have a friend grade all your sections.

Ask your friend to only tell you how many you got wrong in each section.

This means your friend will only tell you that a given section was a -5. They will not tell you anything else about the section.

Go back to each section to find every wrong answer.

The goal is to correct every section to a -0 without using the answer key. 

Send your new answers to your friend to see how much you've improved.

Optional: Repeat this cycle until you get to -0 on each section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Hit List
sequence.text:
6
Hit List
Instructions

Make a spreadsheet with three columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Top 15 Question

Column 2: How This Question Works

Column 3: What I Can Take From This Question

Keep a list of the 15 hardest questions you've ever completed in your prep.

Each day, study two questions from the Hit List.

Dissect exactly how each question is working.

How does the question both camouflage and justify the correct answer?

What makes this question hard?

Figure out what you can take from this question.

And what can you work on in your process to improve your performance on questions that are difficult for the same reason going forward?

Continually add questions to and remove questions from your Hit List as some questions no longer feel difficult and others feel more challenging.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine forces you to look at the section from so many different perspectives all within one intense Routine.

It mixes in stimulus-only practice, answer-choice-only practice, test-day timed practice, and deep review – this refines your process, even when you're already scoring at a high level.

How This Should Be Done

If you need to cap your Thunderdome at 1 hour to complete this Routine within the amount of time you have that's fine. But the deeper you go, the more you'll get out of it.

The Test-Day Timed Sections should cut off when time is called, so they will take up the minority of your time in this Routine, but moving into Party Tricking directly afterwards offers a unique benefit.

Party Tricking is intuition-training and will provide a different perspective on the intuition-based approach that you just utilized in your test-day timed sections.

How to Move On

You can intersperse this Routine with PTs in the last month before your exam.

There's no pressing reason to move on from this Routine since it will always provide a valuable challenge.

You never want to walk into test day with chaos and uncertainty in your veins. SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Abstract Answer Training Regimen exists to fix abstract language Translation problems.

Very often, students will simply skip over or gist abstract language in the answer choices because they don't understand the vocabulary in these answer choices and haven't taken the time to internalize what the complex sentence structuring means.

The Abstract Answer Training Regimen is the opportunity to permanently fix this issue and boost LR and RC accuracy.

How This Should Be Done

You can focus on the Abstract Answer Training Regimen and complete it in a week or less.

Or you can dedicate some time to the Abstract Answer Training Regimen each day for a longer period of time within a larger Routine plan. For instance, you may decide you want to dedicate 30 minutes per day to the Abstract Answer Training Regimen within the context of your larger Routine.

If you're completing the Abstract Answer Training Regimen within the context of a larger Routine, you can progress through the objectives in the Abstract Answer Training Regimen in order, splitting up the objectives between days since you're working with a shorter time span.

For example:

On the first day, memorize the Uncut Method Vocab List.

On the second day, start the Method Vocab Remix.

Whenever you complete the Method Vocab Remix, start the Method/Flaw/Argument Part Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet.

For as long as you're working on the Abstract Answer Training Regimen, continue highlighting words from your sections to add to your Vocab Tracker.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Once you complete all of the objectives in the Abstract Answer Training Regimen, and you are no longer intimidated by abstract language in the answer choices, you can eliminate this Routine from your schedule and return to the other Accuracy Fix Routines.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Stop Oversimplifying
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Stop Oversimplifying

What problem are we solving?

There is no such thing as "just a detail" on the LSAT. 

Ignoring "details" leads to missing question through oversimplifying. If you run with an inaccurate, oversimplified version of the text, you're bound to miss questions.

Answers are right and wrong based on "just one word." That doesn't make the LSAT mean, evil, or unfair. It makes the LSAT a test of precision.

And precision is something you'd to have when you're a lawyer, right? You don't want to be the attorney who harms their client because you missed "just one word." 

Every word on the LSAT deserves equal levels of respect, as it works with every other word to create a conceptual Translation of each sentence.

Conceptual Translation can be the single biggest differentiator between high and lower scorers. It is the opposite of oversimplifying. When you ignore some words in an answer choice and focus solely on other words (keywording), you're not conceptually translating that answer. You're oversimplifying and massively increasing your risk of missing the question.

Keywording reduces an answer's fate solely to whether it has certain words from the stimulus.

However, there are many correct answers that contain no words from the stimulus. There are many wrong answers that contain tons of words from the stimulus. 

You cannot oversimplify answer choice selection to a shallow matching game and expect the LSAT to tolerate it. It won't. 

But this is just one way oversimplification decreases your score. There are approximately one million other ways oversimplification decreases your score. 

This Accuracy Fix trains you to embrace complexity because your mind is strong enough to handle it. Luckily, this is something you were trained to do in the Translation Prep Stage. Now is the time to put that training into action, especially in the answer choices. 

That's how we stop you from missing so many questions.

inline_prep.text:
Accuracy
FIX 2 OF 7
Stop Oversimplifying
Prep Map
/
Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 2 OF 7
Stop Oversimplifying
What Problem Are We Solving?

There is no such thing as "just a detail" on the LSAT. 

Ignoring "details" leads to missing question through oversimplifying. If you run with an inaccurate, oversimplified version of the text, you're bound to miss questions.

Answers are right and wrong based on "just one word." That doesn't make the LSAT mean, evil, or unfair. It makes the LSAT a test of precision.

And precision is something you'd to have when you're a lawyer, right? You don't want to be the attorney who harms their client because you missed "just one word." 

Every word on the LSAT deserves equal levels of respect, as it works with every other word to create a conceptual Translation of each sentence.

Conceptual Translation can be the single biggest differentiator between high and lower scorers. It is the opposite of oversimplifying. When you ignore some words in an answer choice and focus solely on other words (keywording), you're not conceptually translating that answer. You're oversimplifying and massively increasing your risk of missing the question.

Keywording reduces an answer's fate solely to whether it has certain words from the stimulus.

However, there are many correct answers that contain no words from the stimulus. There are many wrong answers that contain tons of words from the stimulus. 

You cannot oversimplify answer choice selection to a shallow matching game and expect the LSAT to tolerate it. It won't. 

But this is just one way oversimplification decreases your score. There are approximately one million other ways oversimplification decreases your score. 

This Accuracy Fix trains you to embrace complexity because your mind is strong enough to handle it. Luckily, this is something you were trained to do in the Translation Prep Stage. Now is the time to put that training into action, especially in the answer choices. 

That's how we stop you from missing so many questions.

How You Know You Need To Do This
Is This Worth My Time?

of

VERDICT:

Not Really Me
You skip over words when you don't know their definitions or they seem "unimportant"
You keyword the answer choices
You say that the author "basically" said X, but X is really not what the author meant at all
You make remarks like "these two answers are the same"
You place Missions in the Low-Density column in your Density Buckets
You often find yourself using referential phrasing like "it," "that," "they," "this," or "the conclusion"
Your internal monologue is vague and filled with referential language

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Decaf RC Translation Drill
≥ 1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Answer Choice Translation Primer
sequence.text:
3
Answer Choice Translation Primer
Instructions

NOTE: You should not break up the individual Answer Choice Translation sections over more than one day, but completing the Answer Choice Primer in its entirety will take 6 prep days if you do one workout per day.

For the first three days, complete new one section* per day of the Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drill (defined below), for a total of three Written sections.

For the next three days, complete one new section per day of the Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drill (defined below), for a total of three Out Loud sections.

Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drills

Make a spreadsheet with two columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Answer Choice Text

Column 2: Translation

Read only the answer choices in the section.

Do not read the stimulus.

Do not read the question stem.

Write down the text of each individual answer choice in the Answer Choice Text column.

Do not copy/paste this text. Type the text yourself.

Write down a Translation of each answer choice in the Translation column.

This means read A, write the literal text of A, and write the Translation of A. Then repeat the same process on B, C, D, and E for each question.

Your Translation of the answer choice cannot be a copy/paste of the answer choice text nor can it be exactly the same as the answer choice text. Translation means putting the same meaning in your own words.

Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drills

Read only the answer choices in the section.

Do not read the stimulus.

Do not read the question stem.

Translate the answer choice out loud.

Quip the answer choice out loud.

This means read A, translate A, and quip A. Then repeat the same process on B, C, D, and E for each question.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The Answer Choice Primer arrives as soon as we hit the Translation + CLIR time goal to transfer our stimulus Translation skills into the answer choices.

The first half of the Primer is super tedious, so be ready. However, it's only tedious because it's stopping you from skipping over words in the answer choices.

The Primer is actually doing you a HUGE favor that you'll (hopefully) never recover from, even if it seems really annoying.

How This Should Be Done

Now that Translation + CLIR has moved to a warmup, lean into upping your Decaf RC Translation volume so that your RC Translation progression doesn't lag too far behind LR.

The more frequently you Decaf, the faster and easier it will become 🪄

Ideally, you are practicing 3 consecutive sections of Decaf RC Translation per day. If you don't practice Decaf every day or don't follow the Decaf instructions, it will stay difficult longer.

The Answer Choice Primer will take several days to complete.

It will feel very slow in the beginning, but make sure you're not trying to speed it up in the wrong ways. Write a real Translation in the Translation column, not just a near-copy/paste of the exact words of the answer choice.

The Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drill is meant to slow you down and get you to acknowledge every word of every answer choice. That said, do not elongate filling in the spreadsheet longer than you have to.

How to Move On

First, complete 3 sections of the Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drill.

After that, complete 3 sections of the Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drill.

There is no time threshold on either drill; completing the sections is what moves you on.

Then move on to the Decaf + LR Translation Routine.

  3. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

  4. Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

  5. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

  6. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

  7. Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

  8. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

  9. Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

  10. Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

sequence.name: Answer Choice Translation Primer
sequence.text:
3
Answer Choice Translation Primer
Instructions

NOTE: You should not break up the individual Answer Choice Translation sections over more than one day, but completing the Answer Choice Primer in its entirety will take 6 prep days if you do one workout per day.

For the first three days, complete new one section* per day of the Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drill (defined below), for a total of three Written sections.

For the next three days, complete one new section per day of the Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drill (defined below), for a total of three Out Loud sections.

Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drills

Make a spreadsheet with two columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Answer Choice Text

Column 2: Translation

Read only the answer choices in the section.

Do not read the stimulus.

Do not read the question stem.

Write down the text of each individual answer choice in the Answer Choice Text column.

Do not copy/paste this text. Type the text yourself.

Write down a Translation of each answer choice in the Translation column.

This means read A, write the literal text of A, and write the Translation of A. Then repeat the same process on B, C, D, and E for each question.

Your Translation of the answer choice cannot be a copy/paste of the answer choice text nor can it be exactly the same as the answer choice text. Translation means putting the same meaning in your own words.

Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drills

Read only the answer choices in the section.

Do not read the stimulus.

Do not read the question stem.

Translate the answer choice out loud.

Quip the answer choice out loud.

This means read A, translate A, and quip A. Then repeat the same process on B, C, D, and E for each question.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Why Are We Doing This?

The Answer Choice Primer arrives as soon as we hit the Translation + CLIR time goal to transfer our stimulus Translation skills into the answer choices.

The first half of the Primer is super tedious, so be ready. However, it's only tedious because it's stopping you from skipping over words in the answer choices.

The Primer is actually doing you a HUGE favor that you'll (hopefully) never recover from, even if it seems really annoying.

How To Pull This Off

Now that Translation + CLIR has moved to a warmup, lean into upping your Decaf RC Translation volume so that your RC Translation progression doesn't lag too far behind LR.

The more frequently you Decaf, the faster and easier it will become 🪄

Ideally, you are practicing 3 consecutive sections of Decaf RC Translation per day. If you don't practice Decaf every day or don't follow the Decaf instructions, it will stay difficult longer.

The Answer Choice Primer will take several days to complete.

It will feel very slow in the beginning, but make sure you're not trying to speed it up in the wrong ways. Write a real Translation in the Translation column, not just a near-copy/paste of the exact words of the answer choice.

The Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drill is meant to slow you down and get you to acknowledge every word of every answer choice. That said, do not elongate filling in the spreadsheet longer than you have to.

How To Move On

First, complete 3 sections of the Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet Drill.

After that, complete 3 sections of the Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drill.

There is no time threshold on either drill; completing the sections is what moves you on.

Then move on to the Decaf + LR Translation Routine.

sequence.name: Answer Choice Warmup
sequence.text:
1
Answer Choice Warmup
Instructions

Open up a previously-seen LR or RC section*.

Translate the first four questions' answer choices in the style of a Written Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet.

Read only the answer choices for these four questions.

Do not read the stimulus or the question stem.

Write down each individual answer choice.

Write down a Translation of each answer choice.

This means read A, write the literal text of A, and write the Translation of A. Then repeat the same process on B, C, D, and E.

Use the same spreadsheet and same style as you used when you completed the Answer Choice Translation Primer.

Translate the next four questions' answer choices in the style of an Out Loud Answer Choice Translation Drill.

Read only the answer choices in the section.

Do not read the stimulus.

Do not read the question stem.

Translate the answer choice out loud.

Quip the answer choice out loud.

This means read A, translate A, and quip A. Then repeat the same process on B, C, D, and E.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

1
Answer Choice Warmup
2
Practice Test (PT)
4 SECTIONS
Instructions

In Self-Paced Mode, open each section of a full PT* in separate tabs in LawHub before you start.

We are opening up separate tabs so we do not have to press Complete Section to go to the next section.

We care about not pressing Complete Section because we want to Camo the PT, rather than having all the correct answers revealed to us at the end of the PT.

Do not use Exam Mode.

Complete section 1 and section 2 with no break in between.

Take a 10 minute break between section 2 and section 3.

Complete section 2 and section 3 with no break in between.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're taking a PT to practice exactly how we will perform on test day. Luckily, the process we use on test day and during PTs has been meticulously honed throughout approximately one million other Workouts you've performed throughout your prep.

This is the PT Routine for all our Answer Choice Translation Primer fans out there. For some test takers, the Answer Choice Translation Primer is an absolute game changer and reviving the Primer on just four questions at a time raises the score on the section, PT, or test day that follows.

Just like the Primer, the Answer Choice Warmup forces you to acknowledge every word of every answer, a great habit to reinforce as you head immediately into answering questions. 

Notice that there is no Camo + Wrong Answer Journal in this Routine. That is because I want you to focus on performance when you take the PT and focus on review when you have enough emotional distance to view your performance objectively (and therefore get much more improvement out of your review).

You might counter that you need to remember your rationale for why you chose an answer when you review and that means you need to review your PT same day.

I would counter that you'll remember your rationale just fine, and this is an excuse so you can rush your review, check your answers, and get the external validation of a score faster. You'll get more out of your PT by spending your subsequent prep day investing in the PT Off Day Routine.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

When you take a PT, make sure that you're treating the experience exactly the same way you treat every other LSAT prep activity you do.

PTs aren't special. Test day isn't special. PTs should not be taken "more seriously" than a Translation Drill, a Mini-Cycle, a Thunderdome, or anything else you do in your prep.

Treat your warmup just as seriously as you treat the PT itself. How you do anything is how you do everything. No breaks between the warmup and the start of the PT. 

When you treat every piece of LSAT preparation with the significance of a PT, you allow even investment across all your practice. This makes a PT much less of a departure from your normal process, which makes the score on the PT less of a departure from your normal score.

The point of taking a PT is to do everything exactly the same way you've practiced. Don't do anything special just because we're calling it a PT.

How to Move On

You don't need to move on! This is the end game.

What problem are we solving?

You should not take an official LSAT until you have practiced regularly in test conditions. This means you're practicing in a quiet environment, taking exactly the allocated time you'll have on test day (no more no less), and you are not taking breaks to go on your phone or talk to people. Practice Test (PT)
4 SECTIONS
Instructions

In Self-Paced Mode, open each section of a full PT* in separate tabs in LawHub before you start.

We are opening up separate tabs so we do not have to press Complete Section to go to the next section.

We care about not pressing Complete Section because we want to Camo the PT, rather than having all the correct answers revealed to us at the end of the PT.

Do not use Exam Mode.

Complete section 1 and section 2 with no break in between.

Take a 10 minute break between section 2 and section 3.

Complete section 2 and section 3 with no break in between.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're taking a PT to practice exactly how we will perform on test day. Luckily, the process we use on test day and during PTs has been meticulously honed throughout approximately one million other Workouts you've performed throughout your prep.

This is the ultimate classic PT Routine. 

The Basic Warm-Up is my personal favorite warm-up and the one that I prescribe most often to my students. Just getting into the flow of Translation + CLIR across an entire section is the perfect way to start a PT regardless of whether or not you have LR or RC first.

I respect that other people like to incorporate both kinds of sections or want a lighter warm-up, and so that's why I vary my PT routines. If I didn't know anything about a person, this Routine is definitely the one that I would give them starting one month before test day. 

Notice that there is no Camo + Wrong Answer Journal in this Routine. That is because I want you to focus on performance when you take the PT and focus on review when you have enough emotional distance to view your performance objectively (and therefore get much more improvement out of your review).

You might counter that you need to remember your rationale for why you chose an answer when you review and that means you need to review your PT same day.

I would counter that you'll remember your rationale just fine, and this is an excuse so you can rush your review, check your answers, and get the external validation of a score faster. You'll get more out of your PT by spending your subsequent prep day investing in the PT Off Day Routine.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

When you take a PT, make sure that you're treating the experience exactly the same way you treat every other LSAT prep activity you do.

PTs aren't special. Test day isn't special. PTs should not be taken "more seriously" than a Translation Drill, a Mini-Cycle, a Thunderdome, or anything else you do in your prep.

Treat your warmup just as seriously as you treat the PT itself. How you do anything is how you do everything. No breaks between the warmup and the start of the PT. 

When you treat every piece of LSAT preparation with the significance of a PT, you allow even investment across all your practice. This makes a PT much less of a departure from your normal process, which makes the score on the PT less of a departure from your normal score.

The point of taking a PT is to do everything exactly the same way you've practiced. Don't do anything special just because we're calling it a PT.

How to Move On

You don't need to move on! This is the end game.

What problem are we solving?

You should not take an official LSAT until you have practiced regularly in test conditions. This means you're practicing in a quiet environment, taking exactly the allocated time you'll have on test day (no more no less), and you are not taking breaks to go on your phone or talk to people. Practicing in chaotic, unplanned conditions causes more score chaos than you'd think.

sequence.name: Mini-Cycle
sequence.text:
2
Mini-Cycle
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

Do not read the stimulus yet.

For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The first step in raising your score is training each of your skills in isolation.

This is what the Mini-Cycle is good at because it breaks the process of answering an LR question down into its component pieces.

We need to train each of your skills in isolation to overcome bad LSAT habits that decrease the score, like skimming, scanning, and gisting. Until we get rid of those habits, the score will stay stuck.

How This Should Be Done

This Routine is intended to be paired with Beginner Accuracy Routine (Day 2) to allow for an alternating every-other-day schedule between the Mini-Cycle and the Acronym. 

This Routine is a tough one to do in 75 minutes, given that the Mini-Cycle can run long. But if you've drilled your Translation + CLIR down to 20 minutes or less, it should be possible. 

Do not check your answers the end of this Routine. Camo on a separate Camo Day.

How to Move On

When the Mini-Cycle breaks the bad habits you may have brought into prep, you can move on from this Routine.

Once you start to see improved accuracy on the Mini-Cycle and you can match that accuracy on Beginner Accuracy Routine (Day 2)'s Acronym LR Sections, you can focus on improving the accuracy through other Accuracy Drills or you can start working on bringing your time down. 

If you see decreased accuracy on the Mini-Cycle, you likely have a stamina issue and can't maintain focus all the way through the workout. If you're seeing better accuracy on the Acronym LR Section in Beginner Accuracy Routine (Day 2), stick with Beginner Accuracy Routine (Day 2) and abandon this Routine. 

If you have 53-minute accommodations or 70-minute accommodations, you do not have to move on from Mini-Cycles as your preferred LR modality since you can do a Mini-Cycle on test day.

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits

What problem are we solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

Instructions

Make a spreadsheet with three columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Vexing Answer Choice

Column 2: Answer Choice Translation

Collect all the difficult answer choices to translate, focusing especially on Method/Flaw/Argument Part answer choices.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The Acronym trains you to perform the full LR process in one fluid motion.

At first, it's going to feel like a lot of steps, but that's why the literal acronym inside the Acronym instructions exists.

The Acronym helps you remember the steps. As you perform this Workout over and over again, those steps start to sink into your body and become involuntary. That's the goal of the Acronym.

Once the steps become involuntary, the score naturally rises because the process takes care of the difficulty. You just take care of the process.

How This Should Be Done

This Routine is intended to be paired with Beginner Accuracy Routine 2 to allow for an alternating every-other-day schedule between the Mini-Cycle and the Acronym. 

Do as much Method/Flaw/Argument Part Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet as you can fit within your 75-minute time block.

How to Move On

Once you hit goal accuracy on your Acronym, you can begin Speed practice. 

Once you no longer have any trouble translating answer choices, you can switch out the Method/Flaw/Argument Part Answer Choice Translation Spreadsheet for another Targeted Accuracy Fix. 

If you see decreased accuracy on the Acronym LR Section versus the Mini-Cycle in Beginner Accuracy Routine (Day 1) and you have 53-minute accommodations or 70-minute accommodations, stick with the Mini-Cycle as your preferred LR modality since you can do a Mini-Cycle on test day. 

If the Mini-Cycle is still performing better than the Acronym and you do not have any of these accommodations, ask yourself what you are doing differently in the Acronym section. Work on porting over the impulse control that the Mini-Cycle enforces.

Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
≥ 3 SECTIONS
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Aeon.co

5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

Instructions

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Hitting the Caffeinated time goal with high retention make the RC question so much easier within time.

RC section will feel feel very different after you meet this time goal.

How This Should Be Done

Caffeinated RC Translation is the endgame RC Translation Drill.

This is what you'll actually do in a 35-minute section, unless you really like Cappuccino RC Translation (35 Version), so we need to ensure we can complete Caffeinated RC Translation at a high quality standard within 4 minutes on average per passage.

In pursuing this 4-minute average time goal, try to not allow passages to deviate from this average time to a large extent.

It's undesirable to have 2-minute passages and equally undesirably to have 6-minute passages, even though these two numbers would average out to 4 minutes.

In general, your Caffeinated RC Translation timing range should be between 3-5 minutes per passage, but limiting the number of passages that get close to 5 minutes.

If you would like additional help meeting this time goal, incorporate a Caffeinated RC Translation Drill Failsafe into your Routine.

At this point in the RC Translation journey, you'll have to learn to trust your memory far more since there are fewer opportunities for recaps.

But you've earned this trust in your memory at this point through all your hard work with Decaf and Cappuccino. In those drills, we verified your memory through the paragraph-level and full-passage recaps.

Now we can trust that you know the passage when you translate it, but we will continue to check in through periodic full-passage recaps just to make sure our standard isn't slipping.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Once your Caffeinated RC Translation Drills are down to 4 minutes per passage, with high-quality recaps throughout, you can move on to the Accuracy Prep Stage.

sequence.name: Translation + CLIR Drill
sequence.text:
1
Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
≥ 3 SECTIONS
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

This is what you'll actually do in a 35-minute section, unless you really like Cappuccino RC Translation (35 Version), so we need to ensure we can complete Caffeinated RC Translation at a high quality standard within 4 minutes on average per passage.

In pursuing this 4-minute average time goal, try to not allow passages to deviate from this average time to a large extent.

It's undesirable to have 2-minute passages and equally undesirably to have 6-minute passages, even though these two numbers would average out to 4 minutes.

In general, your Caffeinated RC Translation timing range should be between 3-5 minutes per passage, but limiting the number of passages that get close to 5 minutes.

If you would like additional help meeting this time goal, incorporate a Caffeinated RC Translation Drill Failsafe into your Routine.

At this point in the RC Translation journey, you'll have to learn to trust your memory far more since there are fewer opportunities for recaps.

But you've earned this trust in your memory at this point through all your hard work with Decaf and Cappuccino. In those drills, we verified your memory through the paragraph-level and full-passage recaps.

Now we can trust that you know the passage when you translate it, but we will continue to check in through periodic full-passage recaps just to make sure our standard isn't slipping.

How To Move On

Once your Caffeinated RC Translation Drills are down to 4 minutes per passage, with high-quality recaps throughout, you can move on to the Accuracy Prep Stage.

sequence.text:
1
Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

1

1 section

Instructions

  1. Start a stopwatch.

  2. Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

  3. Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
≥ 3 SECTIONS
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Mini-Cycle
sequence.text:
3
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section
1 SECTION
ALTERNATE
Instructions
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

Do not read the stimulus yet.

For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Cappuccino RC Translation brings a lighter, more time-efficient RC Translation process that can be used within more test-day timing scenarios.

This Routine ensures that there is no drop in passage retention when we move from Decaf to Cappuccino.

How This Should Be Done

Cappuccino is a much faster drill than Decaf, so you'll have more time to devote to Mini-Cycles and Acronyms in this Routine.

To meet the Cappuccino time goal, repeat at least three sections of Cappuccino RC Translation in a row in this Routine. Do not complete the questions.

To maximize your progress through Cappuccino RC Translation, hold to the recap standard that you built in Decaf RC Translation. If you lower your standard of comprehension and retention, our work is going to waste.

Yes, it's difficult to continue to push yourself to even more ambitious goals with your memory, but it's worth it when you're able to answer the questions in an RC section confidently from memory, without looking back at the passage.

If you feel confident in your Translation skills, feel free to skip straight to the 35-minute version of Cappuccino RC Translation without doing the regular version first.

However, if you feel your standard of comprehension and retention falter in the 35-minute version, return the regular version of Cappuccino RC Translation. Meet the time goal there and then return to the 35-minute version of the drill afterward.

Whenever I say to "alternate" workouts in a Routine, switch which Workout you do each day. For example, if the Routine says, "Alternate: X // Y (1:1)," that means that I should do X on day 1 and then switch to doing Y the next time I do the Routine. The (1:1) numbers signal how many times you should do each Workout before switching to other Workout.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

You can move on to the Caffeinated + LR Translation Routine once your Cappuccino RC Translation Drill speed reaches the time goal, while keeping recaps high-quality throughout.

Cappuccino RC Translation Speed Goals

6 minutes per passage for Cappuccino RC Translation or 4 minutes per passage for Cappuccino RC Translation (35 Minutes Version)

sequence.name: Translation + CLIR Drill
sequence.text:
1
Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
≥ 3 SECTIONS
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Mini-Cycle
sequence.text:
3
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section
1 SECTION
ALTERNATE
Instructions
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

Do not read the stimulus yet.

For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

Cappuccino + LR Sections Routine

Why are we doing this?

Cappuccino RC Translation brings a lighter, more time-efficient RC Translation process that can be used within more test-day timing scenarios.

This Routine ensures that there is no drop in passage retention when we move from Decaf to Cappuccino.

Do these workouts in this order. For real, the order matters.

How to Pull This Off

Cappuccino is a much faster drill than Decaf, so you'll have more time to devote to Mini-Cycles and Acronyms in this Routine.

To meet the Cappuccino time goal, repeat at least three sections of Cappuccino RC Translation in a row in this Routine. Do not complete the questions.

To maximize your progress through Cappuccino RC Translation, hold to the recap standard that you built in Decaf RC Translation. If you lower your standard of comprehension and retention, our work is going to waste.

Yes, it's difficult to continue to push yourself to even more ambitious goals with your memory, but it's worth it when you're able to answer the questions in an RC section confidently from memory, without looking back at the passage.

If you feel confident in your Translation skills, feel free to skip straight to the 35-minute version of Cappuccino RC Translation without doing the regular version first.

However, if you feel your standard of comprehension and retention falter in the 35-minute version, return the regular version of Cappuccino RC Translation. Meet the time goal there and then return to the 35-minute version of the drill afterward.

Whenever I say to "alternate" workouts in a Routine, switch which Workout you do each day. For example, if the Routine says, "Alternate: X // Y (1:1)," that means that I should do X on day 1 and then switch to doing Y the next time I do the Routine. The (1:1) numbers signal how many times you should do each Workout before switching to other Workout.

How to move on

You can move on to the Caffeinated + LR Translation Routine once your Cappuccino RC Translation Drill speed reaches the time goal, while keeping recaps high-quality throughout.

Cappuccino RC Translation Speed Goals

  • 6 minutes per passage for Cappuccino RC Translation or 4 minutes per passage for Cappuccino RC Translation (35 Minutes Version)

Practice Test (PT)
4 SECTIONS
Instructions

In Self-Paced Mode, open each section of a full PT* in separate tabs in LawHub before you start.

We are opening up separate tabs so we do not have to press Complete Section to go to the next section.

We care about not pressing Complete Section because we want to Camo the PT, rather than having all the correct answers revealed to us at the end of the PT.

Do not use Exam Mode.

Complete section 1 and section 2 with no break in between.

Take a 10 minute break between section 2 and section 3.

Complete section 2 and section 3 with no break in between.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're taking a PT to practice exactly how we will perform on test day.

Luckily, the process we use on test day and during PTs has been meticulously honed throughout approximately one million other Workouts you've performed throughout your prep.

The Circle Warmup tunes you up on each individual element of what makes a successful test day.

Personally, I really like the RC Party Tricking element of the Circle Warmup – this aspect of the Circle Warmup tends to uplift students' attention to detail as they head into their PT. If you've learned to love Party Tricking during your prep journey, I highly recommend this PT Routine.

Notice that there is no Camo + Wrong Answer Journal in this Routine. That is because I want you to focus on performance when you take the PT and focus on review when you have enough emotional distance to view your performance objectively (and therefore get much more improvement out of your review).

You might counter that you need to remember your rationale for why you chose an answer when you review and that means you need to review your PT same day.

I would counter that you'll remember your rationale just fine, and this is an excuse so you can rush your review, check your answers, and get the external validation of a score faster. You'll get more out of your PT by spending your subsequent prep day investing in the PT Off Day Routine.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

When you take a PT, make sure that you're treating the experience exactly the same way you treat every other LSAT prep activity you do.

PTs aren't special. Test day isn't special. PTs should not be taken "more seriously" than a Translation Drill, a Mini-Cycle, a Thunderdome, or anything else you do in your prep.

Treat your warmup just as seriously as you treat the PT itself. How you do anything is how you do everything. No breaks between the warmup and the start of the PT. 

When you treat every piece of LSAT preparation with the significance of a PT, you allow even investment across all your practice. This makes a PT much less of a departure from your normal process, which makes the score on the PT less of a departure from your normal score.

The point of taking a PT is to do everything exactly the same way you've practiced. Don't do anything special just because we're calling it a PT.

How to Move On

You don't need to move on! This is the end game.

What problem are we solving?

You should not take an official LSAT until you have practiced regularly in test conditions. This means you're practicing in a quiet environment, taking exactly the allocated time you'll have on test day (no more no less), and you are not taking breaks to go on your phone or talk to people. Practicing in chaotic, unplanned conditions causes more score chaos than you'd think.

What Problem Are We Solving?

You should not take an official LSAT until you have practiced regularly in test conditions. This means you're practicing in a quiet environment, taking exactly the allocated time you'll have on test day (no more no less), and you are not taking breaks to go on your phone or talk to people. Practicing in chaotic, unplanned conditions causes more score chaos than you'd think.

Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Decaf RC Translation Drill
≥ 1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Mini-Cycle
sequence.text:
3
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section
1 SECTION
ALTERNATE
Instructions
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

Do not read the stimulus yet.

For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Now we're ready to put the whole process together into full LR question answering 🎉

Mini-Cycles and Acronyms alternate in this Routine to see which Workout produces higher accuracy and how big of a timing gap we see between them.

This Routine gives us a headstart on the Accuracy Prep Stage (and a sneak preview on which Accuracy Fixes might be relevant to us) while giving us time to beat Decaf once and for all!

How This Should Be Done

It is extremely important that you complete the workouts in this Routine in the order written here.

The order is important to ensure that you can progress in a reasonable time span. (Yes, all Routines are supposed to be done in the order I write them! But can you tell I'm very often disobeyed? This Routine is very often reordered and progress suffers.)

The Mini-Cycles and Acronyms are not more important to complete than the Translation + CLIR warmup and the Decaf RC Translation.

Do not prioritize the Mini-Cycles and Acronyms more than the rest of the Routine just because you're excited to answer questions.

Completing at least one section of Decaf every day is the bare minimum to allow that skill to grow.

Completing a Decaf Marathon at least once per week will make the daily Decaf practice far more smooth and accessible.

Whenever I say to "alternate" workouts in a Routine, switch which Workout you do each day. For example, if the Routine says, "Alternate: X // Y (1:1)," that means that I should do X on day 1 and then switch to doing Y the next time I do the Routine. The (1:1) numbers signal how many times you should do each Workout before switching to other Workout.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

You can move on to the MemAC Routine or Cappuccino + LR Translation Routine once your Decaf RC Translation Drill speed reaches the goal, while keeping recaps high-quality throughout.

Decaf RC Translation Speed Goals

12 minutes per passage out loud (including out loud recaps)

1

Translation + CLIR Drill

1 section

Instructions

  1. Start a stopwatch.

  2. Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

  3. Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

  4. Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

  5. Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

  6. Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Decaf RC Translation Drill
≥ 1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

sequence.name: Mini-Cycle
sequence.text:
3
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section
1 SECTION
ALTERNATE
Instructions
Mini-Cycle
Acronym LR Section

NOTE: Mini-Cycles involve working through full LR sections in batches of 9 questions at a time, without breaks between batches. Do not do less than a full section*.

For questions #1-3, translate and CLIR the stimulus only.

Do not look at the question stem or answer choices yet.

For questions #4-6, Party Trick the answer choices only.

Do not read the stimulus yet.

For questions #7-9, complete the full question according to the straight-through LR Full Question Process.

Return to questions #1-3 and Party Trick them.

After Party Tricking #1-3, relook at the stimulus and change your answer if needed.

Return to questions #4-6 and translate and CLIR.

Choose an answer based on your new understanding of the stimulus.

Note if the answer choice differs from your original Party-Tricked choice.

Repeat this process with the next 9 questions, and then again with the remaining questions in the section. It’s expected that the last batch of questions is less than 9, so you won’t do as many full questions in that batch.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
