sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Mini-Cycles and Acronyms alternate in this Routine to see which Workout produces higher accuracy and how big of a timing gap we see between them.

How To Pull This Off

It is extremely important that you complete the workouts in this Routine in the order written here.

The order is important to ensure that you can progress in a reasonable time span. (Yes, all Routines are supposed to be done in the order I write them! But can you tell I'm very often disobeyed? This Routine is very often reordered and progress suffers.)

The Mini-Cycles and Acronyms are not more important to complete than the Translation + CLIR warmup and the Decaf RC Translation.

Do not prioritize the Mini-Cycles and Acronyms more than the rest of the Routine just because you're excited to answer questions.

Completing at least one section of Decaf every day is the bare minimum to allow that skill to grow.

Completing a Decaf Marathon at least once per week will make the daily Decaf practice far more smooth and accessible.

Whenever I say to "alternate" workouts in a Routine, switch which Workout you do each day. For example, if the Routine says, "Alternate: X // Y (1:1)," that means that I should do X on day 1 and then switch to doing Y the next time I do the Routine. The (1:1) numbers signal how many times you should do each Workout before switching to other Workout.

You can move on to the MemAC Routine or Cappuccino + LR Translation Routine once your Decaf RC Translation Drill speed reaches the goal, while keeping recaps high-quality throughout.

sequence.name: The Island
sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

Click here to go to The Island (scroll to the bottom!)

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

Failsafe Marathon

Instructions

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Failsafe Marathon Routines combine the best of Failsafes with the best of Marathons.

These Routines can be brutal, especially if you don't beat the Failsafe frequently. But the same thing that makes them punishing also makes them effective.

They're a blunt instrument that will change you as a test taker, so they are often relied upon in emergency situations.

When a test date is within one week and you still aren't able to complete the section in time with goal-level accuracy, this is your Routine.

How This Should Be Done

Failsafe Marathons Routines work well to speed up the progress of a Failsafe Routine.

Sometimes, students will see a lot of traction with Failsafes, but the pace of bringing the time down little by little each day can feel limiting, especially with a near-term test date.

Failsafe Marathon Routines are like the "In Case of Emergency Break the Glass" of the Prep Map.

They are harsh, but they will push you harder than almost any other workout.

How to Move On

If you have lost every Failsafe you've attempted in your Failsafe Marathon for three consecutive prep days, here are a few options for what you can try next:

Set a higher baseline natural pace to start your Failsafe Marathon

Replace the Timing Failsafe in this Routine with a Light Failsafe

Replace the Timing Failsafe in this Routine with Pacing Practice

Return to the Accuracy Fix Routines

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Failsafe Marathon, progress to any of the following Speed Routines: Marathon Routine, Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, or Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine. 

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Failsafe Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Failsafe Marathon Routine

Why are we doing this?

Failsafe Marathon Routines combine the best of Failsafes with the best of Marathons.

These Routines can be brutal, especially if you don't beat the Failsafe frequently. But the same thing that makes them punishing also makes them effective.

They're a blunt instrument that will change you as a test taker, so they are often relied upon in emergency situations.

When a test date is within one week and you still aren't able to complete the section in time with goal-level accuracy, this is your Routine.

How to Pull This Off

Failsafe Marathons Routines work well to speed up the progress of a Failsafe Routine.

Sometimes, students will see a lot of traction with Failsafes, but the pace of bringing the time down little by little each day can feel limiting, especially with a near-term test date.

Failsafe Marathon Routines are like the "In Case of Emergency Break the Glass" of the Prep Map.

They are harsh, but they will push you harder than almost any other workout.

How to move on

If you have lost every Failsafe you've attempted in your Failsafe Marathon for three consecutive prep days, here are a few options for what you can try next:

  1. Set a higher baseline natural pace to start your Failsafe Marathon

  2. Replace the Timing Failsafe in this Routine with a Light Failsafe

  3. Replace the Timing Failsafe in this Routine with Pacing Practice

  4. Return to the Accuracy Fix Routines

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Failsafe Marathon, progress to any of the following Speed Routines: Marathon Routine, Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, or Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine. 

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Failsafe Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

1

2
Practice Test (PT)
4 SECTIONS
Instructions

In Self-Paced Mode, open each section of a full PT* in separate tabs in LawHub before you start.

We are opening up separate tabs so we do not have to press Complete Section to go to the next section.

We care about not pressing Complete Section because we want to Camo the PT, rather than having all the correct answers revealed to us at the end of the PT.

Do not use Exam Mode.

Complete section 1 and section 2 with no break in between.

Take a 10 minute break between section 2 and section 3.

Complete section 2 and section 3 with no break in between.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're taking a PT to practice exactly how we will perform on test day. Luckily, the process we use on test day and during PTs has been meticulously honed throughout approximately one million other Workouts you've performed throughout your prep.

This is your PT Routine if you tend to get better scores on the later sections in your prep each day. If you tend to excel later on in your prep day, we need to make sure we get you to your peak performance before the test starts, hence this Routine.

Notice that there is no Camo + Wrong Answer Journal in this Routine. That is because I want you to focus on performance when you take the PT and focus on review when you have enough emotional distance to view your performance objectively (and therefore get much more improvement out of your review).

You might counter that you need to remember your rationale for why you chose an answer when you review and that means you need to review your PT same day.

I would counter that you'll remember your rationale just fine, and this is an excuse so you can rush your review, check your answers, and get the external validation of a score faster. You'll get more out of your PT by spending your subsequent prep day investing in the PT Off Day Routine.

How This Should Be Done

When you take a PT, make sure that you're treating the experience exactly the same way you treat every other LSAT prep activity you do.

PTs aren't special. Test day isn't special. PTs should not be taken "more seriously" than a Translation Drill, a Mini-Cycle, a Thunderdome, or anything else you do in your prep.

Treat your warmup just as seriously as you treat the PT itself. How you do anything is how you do everything. No breaks between the warmup and the start of the PT. 

When you treat every piece of LSAT preparation with the significance of a PT, you allow even investment across all your practice. This makes a PT much less of a departure from your normal process, which makes the score on the PT less of a departure from your normal score.

The point of taking a PT is to do everything exactly the same way you've practiced. Don't do anything special just because we're calling it a PT.

How to Move On

You don't need to move on! This is the end game.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Combining the Circle Warm-Up with the Skeleton Style Thunderdome lets you target your Parallel Reasoning skills before putting them to work in a Test-Day Timed LR Section.

How This Should Be Done

If you haven't brought your timing to test-day levels yet, feel free to switch the Test-Day Timed LR Section for a Write In, Acronym, or other Natural Pace section. 

This Routine can still be effective even if you cut your Skeleton Style Thunderdome down to 10 questions.

Obviously, the more Skeleton Style Thunderdoming you do, the more effective it will be, but any level of independent analogy-building in the Thunderdome setting will be beneficial when you move into the Test-Day Timed LR Section.

How to Move On

You can move on from this Routine when you no longer have any baggage about Parallel Reasoning.

Doing the Skeleton Style Thunderdome practice will allow you to become a lot more comfortable with the process of creating analogies, so you can enter Parallel Reasoning questions with more confidence.

4 SECTIONS
Instructions

In Self-Paced Mode, open each section of a full PT* in separate tabs in LawHub before you start.

We are opening up separate tabs so we do not have to press Complete Section to go to the next section.

We care about not pressing Complete Section because we want to Camo the PT, rather than having all the correct answers revealed to us at the end of the PT.

Do not use Exam Mode.

Complete section 1 and section 2 with no break in between.

Take a 10 minute break between section 2 and section 3.

Complete section 2 and section 3 with no break in between.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're taking a PT to practice exactly how we will perform on test day. Luckily, the process we use on test day and during PTs has been meticulously honed throughout approximately one million other Workouts you've performed throughout your prep.

This PT Routine contains the fastest warmup I've got.

I only recommend this PT Routine for students who still have stamina issues leading into test day or students with really early test-day time slots who need the fastest warmup possible (so they don't have to wake up too early).

The Light Warmup blends stimulus Translation + CLIR with answer choice Translation on RC, getting your feet wet across the entire exam with minimal time expenditure. However, most students benefit from building a little more momentum before the test than this warmup provides.

Notice that there is no Camo + Wrong Answer Journal in this Routine. That is because I want you to focus on performance when you take the PT and focus on review when you have enough emotional distance to view your performance objectively (and therefore get much more improvement out of your review).

You might counter that you need to remember your rationale for why you chose an answer when you review and that means you need to review your PT same day.

I would counter that you'll remember your rationale just fine, and this is an excuse so you can rush your review, check your answers, and get the external validation of a score faster. You'll get more out of your PT by spending your subsequent prep day investing in the PT Off Day Routine.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

When you take a PT, make sure that you're treating the experience exactly the same way you treat every other LSAT prep activity you do.

PTs aren't special. Test day isn't special. PTs should not be taken "more seriously" than a Translation Drill, a Mini-Cycle, a Thunderdome, or anything else you do in your prep.

Treat your warmup just as seriously as you treat the PT itself. How you do anything is how you do everything. No breaks between the warmup and the start of the PT. 

When you treat every piece of LSAT preparation with the significance of a PT, you allow even investment across all your practice. This makes a PT much less of a departure from your normal process, which makes the score on the PT less of a departure from your normal score.

The point of taking a PT is to do everything exactly the same way you've practiced. Don't do anything special just because we're calling it a PT.

How to Move On

You don't need to move on! This is the end game.

Practice Occurs Under Full Test Conditions

What problem are we solving?

You should not take an official LSAT until you have practiced regularly in test conditions. This means you're practicing in a quiet environment, taking exactly the allocated time you'll have on test day (no more no less), and you are not taking breaks to go on your phone or talk to people. Practicing in chaotic, unplanned conditions causes more score chaos than you'd think.

Your Prep Plan

What Problem Are We Solving?

You should not take an official LSAT until you have practiced regularly in test conditions. This means you're practicing in a quiet environment, taking exactly the allocated time you'll have on test day (no more no less), and you are not taking breaks to go on your phone or talk to people. Practicing in chaotic, unplanned conditions causes more score chaos than you'd think.

sequence.name: The Island
sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

Click here to go to The Island (scroll to the bottom!)

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The Marathon Routine is the most effective Routine in the Prep Map for pure speed improvement.

No other Routine or workout will increase speed like this Routine.

The purpose of the Marathon Routine is to decrease the time it takes to get questions right by exhausting you to the point where your subconscious intuition will have to kick in to complete the questions.

This Routine will eventually enable you to finish the section in time at goal accuracy.

How This Should Be Done

Marathons have a ton of specific, crucial instructions, so make sure you internalize the Marathon timing procedures, section data to track, and advice on how to win contained in the Marathon Workout instructions.

When adding Marathon Routines to your prep, be strategic about section usage.

Since one Marathon uses several PTs, you have to stay mindful about your consumption of these non-renewable resources. It can be advisable to mix previously-seen material into some Marathons to minimize material usage.

Make sure you don't Marathon all the most recent PTs; this will leave you with no fresh exams to use as full test-conditions practice tests.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Marathon Routines can get you to test-day goal time and accuracy without progressing to any other Speed Routine.

However, you should change your Speed Routine, if you notice any of the following issues in your Marathon Routine:

Your speed and accuracy on new sections have plateaued or gotten worse for three Marathons in a row

Try a Timing Failsafe Routine or return to the Accuracy Fix Routines

You don't have uninterrupted blocks of time on your calendar for Marathons and you are unwilling to adjust your calendar

Move to a Timing Failsafe Routine

Your score decreases when you switch from LR to RC or RC to LR

Move to a Mixed Section Marathon Routine

If you're still not hitting your time and accuracy goals, or you're just starting to reach your time goals while maintaining accuracy on a few sections, you probably need to do more Marathon Routines.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

SHOW LESS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

Speed
Marathon Routine
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Speed

Marathon Routine

Why are we doing this?

The Marathon Routine is the most effective Routine in the Prep Map for pure speed improvement.

No other Routine or workout will increase speed like this Routine.

The purpose of the Marathon Routine is to decrease the time it takes to get questions right by exhausting you to the point where your subconscious intuition will have to kick in to complete the questions.

This Routine will eventually enable you to finish the section in time at goal accuracy.

LR
RC
FrequencySpaced Set
Challenge IndexEllen Whyyy
LevelAdvanced
Study block4-5+ hours
Time goal to move on20 min

Routine Schedule

Do these workouts in this order. For real, the order matters.

1

The Island

10 minutes
2

Translation + CLIR Drill

1 section
3

Marathon

8 sections
4

Camo Review

5

Wrong Answer Journal

How to Pull This Off

Marathons have a ton of specific, crucial instructions, so make sure you internalize the Marathon timing procedures, section data to track, and advice on how to win contained in the Marathon Workout instructions.

When adding Marathon Routines to your prep, be strategic about section usage.

Since one Marathon uses several PTs, you have to stay mindful about your consumption of these non-renewable resources. It can be advisable to mix previously-seen material into some Marathons to minimize material usage.

Make sure you don't Marathon all the most recent PTs; this will leave you with no fresh exams to use as full test-conditions practice tests.

Marathon Routine Protocols

  • Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

    • If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

  • Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

    • The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

  • Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

  • Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

    • This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

  • Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How to move on

Marathon Routines can get you to test-day goal time and accuracy without progressing to any other Speed Routine.

However, you should change your Speed Routine, if you notice any of the following issues in your Marathon Routine:

  1. Your speed and accuracy on new sections have plateaued or gotten worse for three Marathons in a row

    1. Try a Timing Failsafe Routine or return to the Accuracy Fix Routines

  2. You don't have uninterrupted blocks of time on your calendar for Marathons and you are unwilling to adjust your calendar

    1. Move to a Timing Failsafe Routine

  3. Your score decreases when you switch from LR to RC or RC to LR

    1. Move to a Mixed Section Marathon Routine

If you're still not hitting your time and accuracy goals, or you're just starting to reach your time goals while maintaining accuracy on a few sections, you probably need to do more Marathon Routines.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

1
Medium Warmup
2
Practice Test (PT)
4 SECTIONS
Instructions

In Self-Paced Mode, open each section of a full PT* in separate tabs in LawHub before you start.

We are opening up separate tabs so we do not have to press Complete Section to go to the next section.

We care about not pressing Complete Section because we want to Camo the PT, rather than having all the correct answers revealed to us at the end of the PT.

Do not use Exam Mode.

Complete section 1 and section 2 with no break in between.

Take a 10 minute break between section 2 and section 3.

Complete section 2 and section 3 with no break in between.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're taking a PT to practice exactly how we will perform on test day. Luckily, the process we use on test day and during PTs has been meticulously honed throughout approximately one million other Workouts you've performed throughout your prep.

The Medium Warmup is honestly still pretty light, but it can get you in the zone a little more than the Light Warmup.

This Routine includes translating a full RC passage and answering 5 LR questions. If you want a warmup with minimal time investment and it's important to you to answer full questions, this is the warmup for you. 

Notice that there is no Camo + Wrong Answer Journal in this Routine. That is because I want you to focus on performance when you take the PT and focus on review when you have enough emotional distance to view your performance objectively (and therefore get much more improvement out of your review).

You might counter that you need to remember your rationale for why you chose an answer when you review and that means you need to review your PT same day.

I would counter that you'll remember your rationale just fine, and this is an excuse so you can rush your review, check your answers, and get the external validation of a score faster. You'll get more out of your PT by spending your subsequent prep day investing in the PT Off Day Routine.

How This Should Be Done

When you take a PT, make sure that you're treating the experience exactly the same way you treat every other LSAT prep activity you do.

PTs aren't special. Test day isn't special. PTs should not be taken "more seriously" than a Translation Drill, a Mini-Cycle, a Thunderdome, or anything else you do in your prep.

Treat your warmup just as seriously as you treat the PT itself. How you do anything is how you do everything. No breaks between the warmup and the start of the PT. 

When you treat every piece of LSAT preparation with the significance of a PT, you allow even investment across all your practice. This makes a PT much less of a departure from your normal process, which makes the score on the PT less of a departure from your normal score.

The point of taking a PT is to do everything exactly the same way you've practiced. Don't do anything special just because we're calling it a PT.

How to Move On

You don't need to move on! This is the end game.

sequence.text:

Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

Instructions

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Besides Translation + CLIR Drills, MemAC is responsible for more score improvement amongst my tutoring students than any other Workout.

When you ping-pong between two answers, trying to decide between them, you will often reread each answer, hoping something clicks this time.

Then you'll reread the other answer, hoping something clicks again. And then back to the answer you just left. And then back to the other answer. This sucks, right?

You only cycle read like this because you can't keep both answers in your working memory.

Think of your working memory like a basket.

Most people have a basket the size of an apple. This means that if they want to place something the size of a watermelon in their basket, they must compress the watermelon to make it fit in the basket.

This working memory scarcity makes you want to cut information down to just its barest "most important" components. Because that's what you have room for.

It is the impulse behind the gist. Because if you don't cut that watermelon down, you don't see how it will fit in your basket.

But if your basket were the size of a car, you wouldn't care about the size of the watermelon, right?

MemAC takes your working memory basket from the size of an apple to the size of a car. That's why we do it.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

Now that you've beaten Decaf, you have the skills to take on MemAC, if you're up for the challenge.

You can choose to take on MemAC now or later in your prep if the need arises; it can be a game-changer for persistent accuracy problems.

If you have less than a month left until a non-negotiable test date, you do not have time to do MemAC right now.

Since you are suspending all other workouts besides the Translation + CLIR warmup and MemAC, you are expected to devote 100% of your time to MemAC to accelerate your progress through the workout.

MemAC is by far the most challenging in the beginning, so if you extend out the beginning stage of MemAC by only doing it intermittently, you are predisposing yourself to unnecessarily crashing out.

MemAC will become significantly easier within one week, if you do it with full focus for at least an hour each day.

If you want to make MemAC easier faster, do more than one hour at a time without breaks. It's not worth doing one MemAC question here or there.

How to Move On

Once you beat MemAC Level 5 (🤩🏆🤯), move on to the Cappuccino + LR Translation Routine. You have the option of moving MemAC to a warm up to keep yourself sharp.

MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

  1. Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

    1. Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

  2. To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

    1. For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

  3. Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

  1. Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

    1. Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

  2. After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

  3. Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

  4. Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  4. Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  6. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

  7. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  8. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

  9. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  10. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

  4. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  6. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

  7. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  8. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  4. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  6. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  7. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  4. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  5. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

  6. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  7. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  4. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  6. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

inline_prep.text:
Translation
ROUTINE 5 OF 7
MemAC Routine
Prep Map
/
Translation
TELL ELLEN
ROUTINE 5 OF 7
MemAC Routine
Why Are We Doing This?

Besides Translation + CLIR Drills, MemAC is responsible for more score improvement amongst my tutoring students than any other Workout.

When you ping-pong between two answers, trying to decide between them, you will often reread each answer, hoping something clicks this time.

Then you'll reread the other answer, hoping something clicks again. And then back to the answer you just left. And then back to the other answer. This sucks, right?

You only cycle read like this because you can't keep both answers in your working memory.

Think of your working memory like a basket.

Most people have a basket the size of an apple. This means that if they want to place something the size of a watermelon in their basket, they must compress the watermelon to make it fit in the basket.

This working memory scarcity makes you want to cut information down to just its barest "most important" components. Because that's what you have room for.

It is the impulse behind the gist. Because if you don't cut that watermelon down, you don't see how it will fit in your basket.

But if your basket were the size of a car, you wouldn't care about the size of the watermelon, right?

MemAC takes your working memory basket from the size of an apple to the size of a car. That's why we do it.

How To Pull This Off

Now that you've beaten Decaf, you have the skills to take on MemAC, if you're up for the challenge.

You can choose to take on MemAC now or later in your prep if the need arises; it can be a game-changer for persistent accuracy problems.

If you have less than a month left until a non-negotiable test date, you do not have time to do MemAC right now.

Since you are suspending all other workouts besides the Translation + CLIR warmup and MemAC, you are expected to devote 100% of your time to MemAC to accelerate your progress through the workout.

MemAC is by far the most challenging in the beginning, so if you extend out the beginning stage of MemAC by only doing it intermittently, you are predisposing yourself to unnecessarily crashing out.

MemAC will become significantly easier within one week, if you do it with full focus for at least an hour each day.

If you want to make MemAC easier faster, do more than one hour at a time without breaks. It's not worth doing one MemAC question here or there.

How To Move On

Once you beat MemAC Level 5 (🤩🏆🤯), move on to the Cappuccino + LR Translation Routine. You have the option of moving MemAC to a warm up to keep yourself sharp.

sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Mini-Marathon Routines are a great introduction to speed training, but they are less effective at reducing time than full Marathon Routines.

The purpose of starting Speed practice with Mini-Marathon Routines is to gradually build up the stamina necessary for full Marathon practice, which will allow us to both get faster and exceed the stamina requirements of test day.

If you've been doing Translation + CLIR and Decaf Marathons, you may already have the stamina necessary for full Marathon practice, in which case you can skip this Speed Routine and begin Marathon Routines immediately.

How This Should Be Done

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Why are we doing this?

Mini-Marathon Routines are a great introduction to speed training, but they are less effective at reducing time than full Marathon Routines.

The purpose of starting Speed practice with Mini-Marathon Routines is to gradually build up the stamina necessary for full Marathon practice, which will allow us to both get faster and exceed the stamina requirements of test day.

If you've been doing Translation + CLIR and Decaf Marathons, you may already have the stamina necessary for full Marathon practice, in which case you can skip this Speed Routine and begin Marathon Routines immediately.

Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Mixed Section Marathon Routines are fantastic for students who struggle with context switching and stamina.

If you have any worry about being depleted during the last section on test day, Mixed Section Marathons are better than PTs and standard Marathons for stamina training.

After you've done 1.5x to 2x the sections of a PT in a single sitting with no breaks, it will feel like nothing to do four sections on test day with a break between sections 1 and 2.

How This Should Be Done

Mixed Section Marathons should be approached similarly to regular Marathons, so be sure to familiarize yourself with the Marathon timing procedures, section data to track, and advice on how to win contained in the Marathon Workout instructions.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Mixed Section Marathons are not the most effective Routines for reducing time.

If you are still having trouble meeting you test-day timing goal, you should progress to another Speed Routine that is more suited to pure time reduction (like the Marathon Routine or the Failsafe Marathon Routine).

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Mixed Section Marathon Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.

sequence.name: The Island
sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

3
Mixed Section Marathon
8 SECTIONS
Instructions

Alternate between LR and RC for six to eight sections* total in one sitting with no breaks.

This means that the first section of the Marathon will be LR and the second section will be RC. This 1:1 pattern of LR and RC repeats until the end of the Marathon.

You can choose to alternate the LR and RC sections in any pattern you desire, as suits your needs. For instance, it may be useful to alternate every two sections of LR with one section of RC (2:1:2:1:2).

4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The purpose of Mixed Timing Marathon Routines is to gradually integrate test-day timing standards into your skillset while minimally disrupting accuracy.

By allowing alternation between Marathon timing and test-day timing, you have the opportunity to reaffirm your standards without compromise during the Marathon-timed sections and then get used to pushing those standards into the test-day timing window.

Don't attempt Mixed Timing Marathon Routines if your marathon-timed sections are 10+ minutes from test-day timing.

Mixed Timing Marathons are not typically as effective as regular Marathons at large time reduction (10+ minutes) since the alternation makes it more difficult to reach the flow state required for subconscious skill integration (which is what allows the time to drop).

However, Mixed Timing Marathons are great to ease into how test day will feel.

How This Should Be Done

To make the most of a Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, the variation between Marathon-timed sections and test-day timed sections shouldn't be too great.

You don't want the two kinds of timed sections to feel like a yo-yo (one section with very high timing, followed by another section with very low timing).

Ideally, there isn't much of a difference between the Marathon-timed sections and the test-day timed sections. Since you are never allowed to end sections before your countdown test-day timer expires (35 minutes, 53 minutes, etc), the only time variation you should see between sections is higher times on some of the Marathon-timed sections.

Try to keep Marathon timed-sections to a maximum of 10 minutes over your test-day timed sections.

This advice shouldn't be a reason to continuously check the time during Marathon-timed sections – instead, think of this advice as a caution against jumping into this Speed Routine before you're ready.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

Mixed Timing Marathon Routine

Speed
TELL ELLEN
ROUTINE 6 OF 7
Mixed Timing Marathon Routine
Why Are We Doing This?

The purpose of Mixed Timing Marathon Routines is to gradually integrate test-day timing standards into your skillset while minimally disrupting accuracy.

By allowing alternation between Marathon timing and test-day timing, you have the opportunity to reaffirm your standards without compromise during the Marathon-timed sections and then get used to pushing those standards into the test-day timing window.

Don't attempt Mixed Timing Marathon Routines if your marathon-timed sections are 10+ minutes from test-day timing.

Mixed Timing Marathons are not typically as effective as regular Marathons at large time reduction (10+ minutes) since the alternation makes it more difficult to reach the flow state required for subconscious skill integration (which is what allows the time to drop).

However, Mixed Timing Marathons are great to ease into how test day will feel.

How To Pull This Off

To make the most of a Mixed Timing Marathon Routine, the variation between Marathon-timed sections and test-day timed sections shouldn't be too great.

You don't want the two kinds of timed sections to feel like a yo-yo (one section with very high timing, followed by another section with very low timing).

Ideally, there isn't much of a difference between the Marathon-timed sections and the test-day timed sections. Since you are never allowed to end sections before your countdown test-day timer expires (35 minutes, 53 minutes, etc), the only time variation you should see between sections is higher times on some of the Marathon-timed sections.

Try to keep Marathon timed-sections to a maximum of 10 minutes over your test-day timed sections.

This advice shouldn't be a reason to continuously check the time during Marathon-timed sections – instead, think of this advice as a caution against jumping into this Speed Routine before you're ready.

Marathon Routine Protocols

Warm up before any Marathon-style Routine so you can hit the first section with a running start.

If you don't warm up first, the Marathon will not speed you up as much because it will take you longer to build momentum.

Always Camo + Wrong Answer Journal at the end of a Marathon Routine day to avoid building up too much Camo debt.

The normal "wait at least 24 hours before you Camo" rule does not apply to Marathons.

Never interrupt a Marathon to Camo in between sections.

Camo the Marathon sections in the order of completion.

This means you should Camo the first section of your Marathon first, the second section next, and so on.

Complete the entire Camo + Wrong Answer Journal process for each Marathon section before checking any Marathon scores and before starting the Camo process on another Marathon section. Camo and Wrong Answer Journal each section one at a time.

How To Move On

If your test-day timed sections crash and burn on the Mixed Timing Marathons, but you have hit goal time and accuracy on the Marathon-timed sections before, don't give up hope.

You may just be anxious about the countdown timer on test-day timed sections and need experience to acclimate.

Try progressing to Marathon Routines to ground yourself in your accurate, controlled process that consistently fits within test-day timed constraints without the countdown timer.

If you sometimes hit goal time and accuracy in your Mixed Timing Marathon, progress to a Test-Day Timing Marathon Routine.

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

sequence.text:
1
MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
5 QUESTIONS
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Vocabulary Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Vocabulary Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Finish the passage or stimulus.

Be sure to highlight ALL the words you're unsure of.

If you wouldn't bet money on the definition of the word, that means you are unsure of the definition of that word.

Add the highlighted words to your Vocab Tracker and write in the definitions according to the instructions outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
3
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Write In
sequence.text:
4
Write In
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*. 

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

Write in a correct answer to the question.

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
