sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
6
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
7
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

    1. Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

  5. Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

  6. Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

  7. Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
8
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We've finally beaten Translation, which means we're finally in the Accuracy Prep Stage. 

This is where you shine because we've taken care of a lot of the English trouble, and now your analytical skills get to take full center stage.

Any Accuracy Fix or Speed Routine is now open to you, even though I have one more custom non-native speaker Routine after this one.

Now that you've gone through the intense non-native speaker Translation Process, your skills are going to be much more similar to a native speaker with the uplifted analytical ability that you bring to the table as a non-native speaker. This is often a huge win in the Accuracy Prep Stage.

Make sure to keep your fundamentals strong as you move into answering questions. It will feel different now that you have a much stronger understanding of what all the words mean. Keep up your Vocab Training to continue uplifting your English ability.

We move you into a Write In RC and Write In LR first to keep you grounded in the process and force you to make Missions.

It can feel tempting to jump into the questions excited and disorganized, but we need to make sure we fine-tune your analytical process just as much as you fine-tuned your English process.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

Try to stay focused throughout this entire Routine. Only take breaks after MemAC and before Vocab Training. 

You can omit the Cappuccino RC Translation section if you feel confident in your RC Translation skills and don't need the extra warmup.

Don't rush the Write In. They take as long as they take. We will work on speed later. Work on accuracy now.

How to Move On

Review your wrong answers and judge which Accuracy Fixes are relevant to your mistakes. Pursue those Workouts and Routines to address the mistakes you're seeing.

Camo Review and Wrong Answer Journaling will help you with this process. Also, consider making a Highlight Reel once per week. 

After you've hit goal time and accuracy using the Accuracy Fixes and Speed Routines, move on to the Non-Native Speaker Perform Routine.

sequence.name: MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
sequence.text:
1
MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
5 QUESTIONS
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Vocabulary Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Finish the passage or stimulus.

Be sure to highlight ALL the words you're unsure of.

If you wouldn't bet money on the definition of the word, that means you are unsure of the definition of that word.

Add the highlighted words to your Vocab Tracker and write in the definitions according to the instructions outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
3
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Write In
sequence.text:
4
Write In
1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*. 

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

Write in a correct answer to the question.

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
6
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

sequence.text:
7
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
8
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Accuracy
Intuition, Not Impulse
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Intuition, Not Impulse

What problem are we solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

sequence.name: Vocabulary Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Vocabulary Translation Drill
3 SECTIONS
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Finish the passage or stimulus.

Be sure to highlight ALL the words you're unsure of.

If you wouldn't bet money on the definition of the word, that means you are unsure of the definition of that word.

Add the highlighted words to your Vocab Tracker and write in the definitions according to the instructions outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Translation + CLIR Drill
sequence.text:
2
Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
3
Decaf RC Translation Drill
≥ 1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Keep up the volume of your Vocab Translation Drills and Vocab Training as you add Decaf to this Routine. Adding Decaf might make for longer days, but if you need to, you can decrease the number of Translation + CLIR Drills you're doing or the amount of Extracurricular Reading you're doing to account for the extra time.

How to Move On

When you hit the Decaf time goal silently, you can move to the Non-Native Speaker Intermediate Translation Routine.

I allow non-native English speakers to meet the Translation time goals silently, because English pronunciation tends to hold back speed. But do not let this silent standard decrease your adherence to the process. I

t's really important that you retain all of the conceptual details of each passage and each stimulus. Don't let that go just to move faster.

The whole point of this training is to train your English to LSAT level. We can meet that goal, but we can't meet it if you don't adhere to the Translation retention standard.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
3
Decaf RC Translation Drill
≥ 1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Here is a secret: My non-native English speaker students are my absolute favorites. Y'all inspire me. And I do all my best work for you. 

That's why I made a whole parallel Routine path just for non-native speakers, catering to your particular strengths and weaknesses. I love you. Let's do this. 

This Routine can replace the Translation Foundation Routine in the Translation Prep Stage if you are a non-native English speaker. Feel free to integrate the Non-Native English Speaker Routine Progression in with both the Translation Core Routines and the Accuracy Fix Routines. 

As a non-native speaker, you know that there is one big glaring problem for you when it comes to LSAT: vocab. 

And you may have been told by various naysayers that it's hopeless. That you'll never learn all the words you have to know for the LSAT. And there's no guarantee that any word you study will ever come up on test day. 

As someone who has guided many non-native English speakers who live outside the US to 170+ scores, I will tell you that these naysayers are WRONG. 

You can change your vocab level, and it does matter. You can increase the chance that you will know the words you see on test day.

It'll be difficult. It'll be time-consuming, but you can do it. This Routine and the subsequent Routine Progressions will show you how to achieve that goal.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

Note: this Routine is a modification of the Translation Foundation Routine. Go check out the instructions and notes there to get a full picture before you get started on the Non-Native Speaker Routine.

When you first start doing this Routine, you should spend as much time as humanly possible on Vocab Training.

I put the three Vocabulary Translation Drills and the Extracurricular Reading before the Vocab Training in this Routine to give you the opportunity to harvest words every day. That way you'll always have new, highly relevant words to fuel your practice.

Make sure you've watched the How to Read Hard Passages module of the Loophole Online Course before attempting this Routine or any other non-native speaker Routines. 

Feel free to expand the number of Translation + CLIR Drills to enable you to meet the Translation time goal more quickly. Just make sure that you keep the stable foundation of Vocabulary Translation Drills.

One of the most important things you can do for your LSAT prep is to attempt to create an English immersion environment for as much of the day as possible.

I recognize that this can be challenging if you don't live in an English-speaking nation, but please ask your family to help you with this goal. Seek out native English speaker friends and English-language environments. In addition, ask your family if they would try to speak English with you as much as possible.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

When you hit halfway to your Translation + CLIR time goal, move to the Non-Native Speaker Advanced Beginner Translation Routine.

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
3
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
sequence.text:
1
MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

  3. Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

  4. At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

  5. OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

    1. This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

  6. Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

It often takes a fair amount of time for non-native English speakers to reach the Translation + CLIR time goal.

So we have many Routine progressions while you're still working on that Translation + CLIR time goal. In this one, we add MemAC to the mix.

Non-native speakers, especially those who currently live in China or South Korea, tend to excel on MemAC, as the education systems in these nations build exceptional memory skills. 

I'm adding MemAC earlier for you than I do for native English speakers because y'all tend to have a great capacity for it.

Don't despair if it's taking you longer to meet those Translation + CLIR time goals. That's expected; it's part of the plan. When you do meet those time goals (and you WILL), you are going to be unstoppable with accuracy. 

You should be finding fewer words in your Vocabulary Translation Drills these days, and your Vocab Training should be getting simpler.

In addition, Caffeinated RC Translation will not take nearly as long as Cappuccino so you'll have more time for MemAC. But if you haven't met the Cappuccino time goals on the previous Routine, feel free switch out the Caffeinated RC Translation for Cappuccino. There's no pressure to only do Caffeinated here.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

The same Translation time goals advice I shared in the Non-Native Speaker Intermediate Translation Routine about meeting the Translation time goals applies here. 

You will likely need to pair this Routine with Translation Marathons once or twice per week to bring your Translation + CLIR time down to the time goal.

Just to review in case you missed it anywhere else, here are the Translation + CLIR Goals:

The time goal for Translation + CLIR Drills is 20 minutes.

The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations.

Meeting this Translation + CLIR Drill time goal is only valid under two conditions:

You have a CLIR for every stimulus.

You have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section out loud.

MemAC takes a fair number of hours to master, but it is something you can cram and get better really fast. 

If you're willing to spend 6 hours on MemAC (and man, it is only my non-native speaker students who ever will do this! ❤️), you could take half of it out in one single day. You just have to be strong and get through it.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

When you hit the Translation + CLIR time goal, proceed to the Non-Native Speaker Accuracy Routine.

Congratulations on beating Translation as a non-native English speaker. You're an absolute champion. I admire you.

If you haven't beaten MemAC by the time you hit the Translation + CLIR time goal, you can continue your same MemAC practice schedule in the Non-Native Speaker Accuracy Routine, even though that Routine is going to say to move MemAC to a 5 question warmup.

sequence.name: MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
sequence.text:
1
MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Vocabulary Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Finish the passage or stimulus.

Be sure to highlight ALL the words you're unsure of.

Add the highlighted words to your Vocab Tracker and write in the definitions according to the instructions outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Now you've been doing Vocabulary Translation Drills and Vocab Training long enough that we can switch our emphasis from Vocabulary Translation Drills to Translation + CLIR Drills in a focused attempt to meet our Translation + CLIR time goal silently. 

We're moving to Cappuccino in this Routine to bring down our RC Translation time, mimicking the same progression you would make in the Translation Core Routines.

We're adding a Proto-Stimulus Rebound to our Vocabulary Translation Drills in order to more deeply ingrain the memory of the stimulus in your subconscious.

Non-native speakers are typically good with these memory-powered workouts, so the Proto-Stimulus Rebound shouldn't be a time sink. If it is a massive challenge, that just proves that we really needed to do it. Keep it up, and you will improve. 

If any native English speakers are reading this:

Please do not take the silent accommodation I am making here for non-native speakers as a license to meet your Translation + CLIR time goals silently.

Non-native English speakers have a very different experience speaking English out loud, especially when they have never lived in English-speaking nations. The standard is different for a reason.

SHOW LESS
How This Should Be Done

You will likely need to pair this Routine with Translation Marathons once or twice per week to bring your Translation + CLIR time down to the time goal.

Just to review in case you missed it anywhere else, here are the Translation + CLIR Goals:

The time goal for Translation + CLIR Drills is 20 minutes.

The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations.

Meeting this Translation + CLIR Drill time goal is only valid under two conditions:

You have a CLIR for every stimulus.

You have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section out loud.

How to Move On

Once you feel like the Proto-Stimulus Rebound on the Vocabulary Translation Drill is easy, move on to Non-Native Speaker Intense Translation Routine.

1
Vocabulary Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

sequence.name: MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
sequence.text:
1
MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
5 QUESTIONS
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Vocabulary Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Translate and quip the passage or stimulus*.

If you encounter a word you are unsure of, highlight it.

Finish the passage or stimulus.

Be sure to highlight ALL the words you're unsure of.

If you wouldn't bet money on the definition of the word, that means you are unsure of the definition of that word.

Add the highlighted words to your Vocab Tracker and write in the definitions according to the instructions outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video.

Restart the Vocabulary Translation Drill on the same stimulus or passage now that you know what the words mean.

Continue this pattern for the entire section.

sequence.name: Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
3
Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
6
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
7
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
8
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're almost at test day!

This Routine picks up where the Non-Native Speaker Accuracy Routine left off by incorporating Test-Day Timed Sections into the mix.

We're still keeping up our Vocab Training and Vocabulary Translation Drills because honestly vocab practice never ends. You can always get better. There are always more words to learn. (That goes for me too.) 

But your Vocab Translation Drills should hopefully feel like regular Translation + CLIR Drills most of the time these days.

How This Should Be Done

You can omit the 5 questions of MemAC or the Caffeinated Translation Drill warmup if you need a more streamlined Routine or would like to add Targeted Accuracy Fixes to the Routine. 

Stay critical in your Camo + Wrong Answer Journal practice. Always wait 24+ hours before you Camo so that you can approach your results more objectively.

How to Move On

You don't necessarily have to move on from this Routine as long as you intersperse it with PT Routines as you move closer to test day. 

This Routine should function as a good support infrastructure for your PT Routines and Speed Routines. 

But you should be really proud of how much you've accomplished. And just know, I'm rooting for you 💃🏻💚.

1

MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)

5 questions

Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

  1. Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

    1. Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

  2. To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

    1. For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

  3. Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

  1. Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

    1. Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

  2. After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

  3. Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

  4. Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

MemAC Level 1: One answer at a time

When you beat Level 1, progress to Level 2.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Repeat the Translation of A from memory.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  4. Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  6. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

  7. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  8. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

  9. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  10. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 2: Two answers at a time

When you beat Level 2, progress to Level 3.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Repeat the Translation of A and B from memory.

  4. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  6. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

  7. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  8. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 3: Three answers at a time

When you beat Level 3, progress to Level 4.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  4. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C from memory.

  5. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  6. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  7. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

When you beat Level 4, progress to Level 5.

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  4. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

  5. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D from memory.

  6. Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

  7. Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 5: Five answers at a time

When you beat Level 5, congratulations! You've beaten MemAC!

  1. Read, translate, and quip answer choice A.

  2. Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

  3. Read, translate, and quip answer choice C.

  4. Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

sequence.name: Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
3
Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
6
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
7
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
8
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

sequence.name: Hit List
sequence.text:
3
Hit List
Instructions

Make a spreadsheet with three columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Top 15 Question

Column 2: How This Question Works

Column 3: What I Can Take From This Question

Keep a list of the 15 hardest questions you've ever completed in your prep.

Each day, study two questions from the Hit List.

Dissect exactly how each question is working.

How does the question both camouflage and justify the correct answer?

What makes this question hard?

Figure out what you can take from this question.

And what can you work on in your process to improve your performance on questions that are difficult for the same reason going forward?

Continually add questions to and remove questions from your Hit List as some questions no longer feel difficult and others feel more challenging.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Highlight Reel
sequence.text:
4
Highlight Reel
Instructions

Look back over your Wrong Answer Journal.

Based on your past performance, write the top five things you want to do and remember in your LSAT practice moving forward.

Your top five things could include productive habits like always making a Mission on every question. They could also include ideas you want to remember like the three valid Some/Most Inferences.

Your Highlight Reel is your moment for introspection every week to identify the top places you see yourself stumbling in your prep and write how you want to address those places.

You can have a separate Highlight Reel for LR, RC, and for performance mindset, if you want. Otherwise, you can just have one Highlight Reel.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We do this Routine to improve your PT or section performance rather than just repeating your PT or section performance. By identifying the actions you took that caused you to miss questions, you enable yourself to change those actions (and raise the score). 

Despite this Routine's name, feel free to do it even when you're still taking stopwatch-timed or test-day timed sections. This Routine can be really useful even when you have not yet taken PTs.

How This Should Be Done

This Routine should be done at least one day after you've completed a PT. Take your time and focus on your review.

Feel free to add extra Targeted Accuracy Fixes to this Routine. You can add on any Workout that pushes you to change any aspect of your process that was problematic during your PT. 

Put your Highlight Reel on the wall of your study room. Review your Highlight Reel every day before starting your practice and on the morning of test day. 

If you are doing this Routine more than once per week, update your Highlight Reel each time rather than making an entirely new Highlight Reel every time you review a PT.

The scores you get on an experimental section in LawHub matter just as much as scores on regular sections in LawHub. LSAC re-ordered and recombined every PT's sections when they got rid of Logic Games, so the experimental sections you see on LawHub are just scrambled real sections. 

The experimental sections on each PT need review, just like the scored sections. The experimental sections on LawHub are real LSAT sections from real exams given on test day.

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
1
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
2
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

sequence.name: Hit List
sequence.text:
3
Hit List
Instructions

Make a spreadsheet with three columns, or use this template:

Column 1: Top 15 Question

Column 2: How This Question Works

Column 3: What I Can Take From This Question

Keep a list of the 15 hardest questions you've ever completed in your prep.

Each day, study two questions from the Hit List.

Dissect exactly how each question is working.

How does the question both camouflage and justify the correct answer?

What makes this question hard?

Figure out what you can take from this question.

And what can you work on in your process to improve your performance on questions that are difficult for the same reason going forward?

Continually add questions to and remove questions from your Hit List as some questions no longer feel difficult and others feel more challenging.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Highlight Reel
sequence.text:
4
Highlight Reel
Instructions

Look back over your Wrong Answer Journal.

Based on your past performance, write the top five things you want to do and remember in your LSAT practice moving forward.

Your top five things could include productive habits like always making a Mission on every question. They could also include ideas you want to remember like the three valid Some/Most Inferences.

Your Highlight Reel is your moment for introspection every week to identify the top places you see yourself stumbling in your prep and write how you want to address those places.

You can have a separate Highlight Reel for LR, RC, and for performance mindset, if you want. Otherwise, you can just have one Highlight Reel.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Learn From Your Mistakes
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Learn From Your Mistakes

What problem are we solving?

Seeing the score is like popping a balloon. 

You want to see the score so bad. Because you need to "see how you're doing," "understand where you are," "stay motivated," and "know what to work on."

So, of course, you need to check the score as soon as you're done with the section.  But suddenly, as soon as you see that number.

There's nothing interesting left anymore. 

Now you "know where you are," but the emotional reaction to where you are overwhelms any hope of strategic insights. 

If you like the number, you'll walk away excited and think, "Okay, now I'm good."

And then the next section is likely to crash and burn from laziness and complacency. You don't need to work that hard when you're good, right? 

If you don't like the number, tears follow.

Now there's no motivation to continue because nothing ever works. So what's the point? Why try? I should just give up and save the effort I would waste on this. I never get better. 

When you do this, you actively decline to change the behaviors that caused your wrong answers. This causes you to not improve.

Failing to look inward to understand what you need to change will cause you to leave points on the table.

This Accuracy Fix stops that rollercoaster of pain and plateaus.

You can get better. Give yourself the chance to really understand what you're doing wrong.
