MemAC (Memory Answer Choice Translation)
Instructions

NOTE: MemAC is a multi-day series of workouts using previously-seen LR and RC sections that progress through five levels as you meet certain benchmarks. Each level and benchmark is defined below. MemAC can be completed as a full section* or by completing as much MemAC as possible in 1-3 hour blocks.

Start MemAC at Level 1, or from wherever you left off previously.

Level 1 MemAC means that you will be performing the answer choice Translation process defined in the Level 1 instructions below. If you are on a later Level, follow the corresponding instructions below.

To Level Up: Complete the full MemAC process defined in your Level instructions without having to peek at the answer choices to accurately remember them on 10 questions in a row.

For example, if you correctly recap all the answer choices on 10 questions in a row without having to peek on Level 1, move to Level 2 on the next question.

Each time you complete one full section of MemAC, complete a MemAC Live Check-In Question(defined below).

MemAC Live Check-In Question

Complete a full LR question according to the Full LR Process. 

Just translate and quip the answers normally. Do not do MemAC.

After choosing your answer, attempt to translate all the answer choices from memory. 

Write down how many answers you're able to translate from memory on each Live Check-In Question.

Compare the number of answers you're able to translate from memory across all your Live Check-In Questions to measure your progress.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice E.

Repeat the Translation of A, B, C, D, E from memory.

MemAC Level 4: Four answers at a time

Read, translate, and quip answer choice B.

Read, translate, and quip answer choice D.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine addresses the memory-blanking issue that afflicts many students throughout the LSAT.

If you find yourself getting into the answer choices, but forgetting the stimulus, even though you've properly translated it, this Routine will fix that memory issue.

It's really an under-reported story how much of excellence on the LSAT comes down to working memory capacity and it's sad that most people think they can't improve their working memory.

I know that you can improve your working memory, and I know that this Routine will help you do so. Don't give up even though it might be hard sometimes. You're getting better and it matters.

How This Should Be Done

You can approach this Routine while you're still attempting to beat MemAC Level 5, or as a refresher after you've beaten MemAC Level 5. It'll work out your working memory either way. 

You can customize the amount of MemAC to make the length of this Routine work for you. You can do up to a full section of MemAC, as little as 10 questions of MemAC, or you can cap MemAC at 30/60 minutes. More MemAC is more effective, but do what works for you.

How to Move On

When you're remembering all the details on your Stimulus Rebound and it is no longer challenging, you can move on to another Accuracy Fix Routine.

Accuracy
Strengthen Your Working Memory
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Strengthen Your Working Memory

What problem are we solving?

You know that feeling when your memory just goes blank in the middle of a question? And you kinda have no idea what you're supposed to do?

Yeah, that's not supposed to happen.

That's something to train out of you.

And this whole LSAT thing is going to feel so much better when you have the evidence you need to make the correct decisions in the moment. 

I never knew memory was such privilege and advantage. 

I used to think, "Of course everyone is subconsciously and instantaneously interrelating every answer choice with the compete conceptual idea behind the stimulus. That's the only way anyone would ever make a decision about an answer choice, right?"

WRONG.

This is the blindspot you have when you "just know" the answer to questions.

Choosing answers the way I just described feels so good that you can't imagine anyone would ever want to do it a different way.

But if you don't remember the complete conceptual idea behind the stimulus/passage while you're in the answer choices, you don't have the option of choosing answers this way.

That's the problem what we're here to solve.

This Accuracy Fix will train your memory to be able to enact this (much more fun and accurate) process in the answer choices.

Yes, the training is strenuous, but all good training is. And on the other side, you won't be able to believe you really chose answers without keeping the whole Translation in your working memory.

sequence.text:
3
Decaf RC Translation Drill
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine will make RC far less traumatic.

Translating the question stems one-by-one without having to worry about getting the right answer is so soothing. And then moving into Modified Inside Out, which is essentially an RC section with a bunch of spoilers, keeps your blood pressure at a totally manageable level. 

Specifying that the Modified Inside Out should be done with Decaf is not a way to punish you; it's a way to empower you.

When you finish your Decaf and can actually say out the full recap of the passage without looking, you're going to feel so confident heading into the questions.

That kind of confidence is addictive. You're working toward achieving that confidence with all your other RC practice after this.

How This Should Be Done

Slow and steady wins the race. Don't rush yourself through this Routine. If it takes whatever number of hours, it takes whatever number of hours. Who cares? You did it.

Pressuring yourself for RC speed before you feel comfortable with the section is the number one way students sabotage themselves before they get the chance to build any confidence. Take it at your pace. Don't rush. Speed comes after accuracy.

How to Move On

If you feel less fear (but still a little bit of fear) toward RC, move on to the RC Get to Know You Routine, the next Routine in the I'm Afraid of RC Routine Progression.

If you don't feel any fear toward RC, move on to any of the I Just Want to Focus on RC Routine Progressions.

Accuracy
Stop Mental and Physical Self-Sabotage
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Stop Mental and Physical Self-Sabotage

What problem are we solving?

Have you ever done a section when:

  • you're falling asleep in the middle? 

  • someone else is taking a call a little too close to you? 

  • you're looking at the clock over and over again and saying to yourself "I have to speed up"?

  • you're saying to yourself, "I can't get this wrong. Oh my god, I don't understand. I have to get it. I'll never get into Berkeley. My dad is right about me."?

  • you just saw a previous score and you're going to cry?

  • you have a stye on your left eye and also maybe COVID?

Doing the LSAT like this is mental and physical self-sabotage.

You are willfully engaging in behaviors that decrease your score. 

I care about you and I care about your score, so I'm going to give you some real talk here.

Telling yourself you can't do something drastically increases the chances you won't be able to do that thing.

So stop it. 

Doing LSAT in an environment or situation that pulls on your attention sets you up to fail.

So stop it.

Thinking about the past, the future, and what other people think while you're doing the LSAT ensures that you do not do your best.

So stop it.

This is your Olympics.

We need you in peak mental and physical condition while you're training to ensure that you're in peak condition on test day. This means that you have to advocate for yourself.

Create space in your life for LSAT is to be the #1 priority, not something you do after every high priority is done.

This Accuracy Fix teaches you how to be that your advocate.

I care about you and I care about your score, so I'm going to give you some real talk here.

So stop it.

So stop it.

Thinking about the past, the future, and what other people think while you're doing the LSAT ensures that you do not do your best.

So stop it.

This is your Olympics.

sequence.name: Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Caffeinated RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

At the end of the passage, confirm your Translation with the entire passage. This should take 15-30 seconds.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Caffeinated RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: RC HIIT (High Intensity Interval Training)
sequence.text:
2
RC HIIT (High Intensity Interval Training)
Instructions

Translate the passage*

RC HIIT Phase 1: Complete the following RC Thunderdome outputs in under 30 seconds each before beginning the questions. These outputs may require looking at the passage.

Outline the structure of the passage overall.

You can use paragraphs as an organizing structure, but you can also delineate on a more fine-grained level, if desired.

Parallel one piece of the passage.

Pick an example, one line of reasoning, or a given person's point of view.

Sub out one word in the passage and replace it with a new word/phrase that means the same thing.

Pick one sentence out of the passage and identify its function.

What is the Main Point?

RC HIIT Phase 2: Complete the following RC Thunderdome outputs in under 30 seconds each. You have two options in how you complete the Phrase 2 outputs: You may complete all the additional RC Thunderdome outputs before beginning the questions or complete two to three additional RC Thunderdome outputs in between each of the questions. These outputs do not require you to look at the passage.

What is the tone of the passage?

Who is the author?

Who is the audience?

Who are the players in the passage and what do they believe?

Strengthen the author's opinion

If the passage feels neutral, write a confirming piece of evidence for the information the author is presenting.

Weaken the author's opinion

If the passage feels neutral, write a disconfirming piece of evidence for the information the author is presenting.

One Inference from the passage

One thing the author is likely to believe

Identify a principle underlying the passage as a whole or an argument within the passage

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We pair the depth of RC HIIT with the intuitive movement of the Reverse Shuffle to balance this advanced RC skill workout.

This Routine challenges your speed and agility across all your RC skills. 

Keeping the passage in your working memory while independently pivoting into a new question type every 30 seconds (or less) is no easy task.

Successfully completing this Routine means you're ready for anything, no passage phases you, difficulty doesn't bother you, and you have test day locked down.

How This Should Be Done

Go straight from the RC HIIT into the Reverse Shuffle.

It should feel kinda like a sauna + cold plunge (not that I've ever done that, but I imagine that's what this would feel like).

In the RC HIIT, you'll be burning hot, pulling every insight you can out of the passage. Then in the Reverse Shuffle you have to fly free, trusting your memory to guide you without overthinking. It's a really cool feeling.

Don't overdo this Routine; don't perform it more than once every other day at maximum.

How to Move On

You don't really need to move on from this Routine since it can be useful as an intermittent check-in all the way up through test day.

sequence.name: Party Tricking Jail
sequence.text:
2
Party Tricking Jail
Instructions

NOTE: Party Tricking Jail is an advanced workout for those who want to push themselves to become true answer choice experts. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before entering Party Tricking Jail.

Party Trick every question in an LR or RC section*.

This means you will only read the question stem and answer choices on each question before you select an answer on that question.

Do not look at the stimulus or passage.

Camo the section immediately after completing it.

The Camo will display all the questions that are wrong plus an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Do not look at the stimulus when you Camo.

Party Trick the returned questions again. Doubt your answers on the questions Camo displays and try to correct your answer.

Get as close to -0 on the Camo as you can.

OPTIONAL: Do not exit Party Tricking Jail until you reach -5 or better pre-Camo.

You can customize this accuracy goal to your personal needs.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
3
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We go to Party Tricking Jail when you've become good the LSAT, but not quite great at the LSAT. 

I'll often assign Party Tricking Jail when my students hit a plateau of around -4 on either LR or RC. These students have tried everything, worked hard, but they aren't quite natural at the exam yet.

Often these students will be hardworking technicians who earnestly apply all the methodologies to the absolute best of their ability, but something just hasn't clicked. Party Tricking Jail is what makes the LSAT click (when you give it a real chance).

Yes, it's hard in the beginning. Yes, you have to show a little bit of resilience when you see low accuracy on the first few sections.

But on the other side, you'll have a hard time believing you ever did the LSAT without being able to Party Trick at goal level.

How This Should Be Done

Feel free to customize the Party Tricking Jail goal accuracy to suit your needs.

In general, you should set the Party Tricking Jail goal accuracy to allow for 3-4 more questions wrong than your test-day goal accuracy. For instance, if your goal is -5 on LR/RC on test day, you could set your Party Tricking goal accuracy at -8 or -9. 

Take your Camo really seriously while you're in Party Tricking Jail.

The real challenge of Party Tricking Jail comes in Camo. Do not just stick with your original answer because you don't have any additional information. You do have additional information: You now know that the answer you chose is under suspicion because only a limited number of decoys will come up in Camo.

So if you have any doubt as to your answer, it's time to re-evaluate the answer choices with the added knowledge that you should be suspicious of your original Party Trick answer. You can improve a lot from revisiting the list of questions you've already Party Tricked before you've had the stimulus spoiled.

The goal of the Camo pass in Party Tricking Jail is always to get a -0.

If you're not changing your answers on enough questions to get a -0, you are not improving as much as you can from Party Tricking Jail.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Move on from Party Tricking Jail when you hit your accuracy goals.

If you do a section or two and have worse than 50% accuracy, that is not a reason to give up and move on from Party Tricking Jail.

It's completely expected that you will not have amazing accuracy the first time you try a full section of Party Tricking Jail. That's where the Workout starts. 

Your RC Party Tricking accuracy will be better than your LR Party Tricking accuracy because RC is inherently easier to Party Trick (you gain clues from the other questions). This is not a sign that there is anything wrong with you or that you need to stop doing the Workout.

Accuracy
Don't Be Desperate in the Answers
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Don't Be Desperate in the Answers

What problem are we solving?

Sometimes you just want to get the question right so badly that every answer choice looks like an escape hatch.

"Is it right? Is it right!??

If it's right, then I can move on.

Then I won't waste any more time.

Then the stimulus must have meant this.

Then this must have been what they were looking for."

Notice the desperation dripping off this monologue. 

You're looking for an answer choice to rescue you, but actually the roles need to be reversed. You have to be the strong one.

Be for real. You are better than 80% wrong. 

Answer choices are designed to exploit your desire for them to be right and to prey on moments of inattention.

But you can channel your desire to get the question right into building an invulnerable fortress of analysis throughout every stage of the question. This fortress (Translation, CLIR, Mission, Back Up Plan) will allow you to see exactly why these answers are wrong without. any. drama.

The answer choices only gain manipulative power over you when you look to them to save you. But you are not the freaking damsel that answer C is here to rescue. You're the hero.

You're here to judge answer C, and you're going to judge it according to your vetted, bulletproof standards.

The answers need to impress you, not the other way around.

This Accuracy Fix trains you to build the fortress.

Because you are smart enough. You have the tools, the time, and the resources to never need any answer choice to save you again.

Instructions

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine purposefully messes with the passage and the answer choices to get you to wake up and stop auto-piloting your way through them.

The Reverse Shuffle will hopefully show you how powerful your memory and intuition can be.

Since the E Blackout removes one of the answers, it forces you to trust your knowledge of the passage on a much deeper level. When you can't compare all the answers and settle, you have to really understand what makes an RC answer choice correct.

This Routine is built to break down every second-guessing, answer-choice-settling habit you have.

How This Should Be Done

Students are often desperate to break a plateau, but they aren't desperate to change their habits.

Take the process disruption in this Routine as an opportunity to get you out of any funks you've been in. This Routine is designed to make you re-examine the parts of the process you've taken for granted.

Don't be put off by the uncertainty inherent in the E Blackout or the Reverse Shuffle. The uncertainty is the point because it helps you grow your trust in yourself.

How to Move On

This is a good Routine to return to intermittently when your process starts to get sloppy.

There's no need to move on from this Routine permanently since it can be useful even in the week of your test to offer an answer choice tune-up. 

None of my tutoring students have ever gotten better than a -3 on an RC E Blackout. Hit me up on Tell Ellen if you beat them.

sequence.name: Time Awareness Training
sequence.text:
1
Time Awareness Training
Instructions

NOTE: Checking the time excessively during the exam is a major cause of accuracy issues. This Workout is designed to help you overcome the need to check the time by enhancing your intuitive understanding of how much time has passed.

Look at the clock and note the exact time with seconds.

Aim to look at the clock again exactly when your Time Goal has elapsed.

Five minutes is the Level 1 Time Goal, so start here on your first Time Awareness Training.

If you've done Time Awareness Training before, start at the last Time Goal you've earned.

When you think your Time Goal has elapsed, look at the clock.

You may only look at the clock once per Time Awareness Training.

If you look at the clock within one minute of your Time Goal, progress your Time Goal to the next Level tomorrow.

To progress to the next level of Time Awareness Training, you must check the clock within only one minute of your Time Goal.

If you've checked the time within one minute of the Level 5 Time Goal, congratulations! You've graduated from Time Awareness Training.

If you look at the clock farther than one minute from your Time Goal, this round of Time Awareness Training is now over.

Please restart Time Awareness Training with the same Time Goal tomorrow.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Pacing Practice
sequence.text:
3
Pacing Practice
Instructions

Choose an interval time goal.

Your interval time goal is your target time for each question.

For example, an interval time goal may be 90 seconds per question.

Follow the procedures of How to Set a Realistic Interval Time Goal below.

Set an interval timer to repeatedly countdown from that time goal 30 times in a row.

Do not incorporate rest intervals.

We choose 30 times so we can have some extra intervals in case our timer messes up.

Start your interval timer when you begin an LR or RC section*.

For RC, only use the interval timer on the questions, not during the passage.

You must select an answer on each question before the interval timer goes off.

You cannot stay on a question longer than the interval timer permits, no matter how badly you want to.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine eases you in to timing with minimal traumatic events. 

By doing this Routine before jumping into Test-Day Timed Sections, you enable yourself to more effectively transition your goal accuracy into a timed environment.

By studying and understanding timing on a deeper level, you train yourself to be fast as opposed to just expecting yourself to be fast.

How This Should Be Done

Gradually build up your Time Awareness Training as you progress through this Routine.

You have the option of overlapping your Time Awareness Training with other tasks as noted in the Time Awareness Training instructions, but make sure to go directly into the Cappuccino warmup and RC Pacing Practice as soon as the Time Awareness Training is completed.

This will enable you to more effectively and intuitively feel the time during your RC Pacing Practice.

How to Move On

You can move on from this Routine when you no longer feel the urge to check the clock to know how much time has passed.

I want you to trust yourself and your own internal clock so that you don't distract yourself on test day.

sequence.name: Time Awareness Training
sequence.text:
1
Time Awareness Training
Instructions

NOTE: Checking the time excessively during the exam is a major cause of accuracy issues. This Workout is designed to help you overcome the need to check the time by enhancing your intuitive understanding of how much time has passed.

Look at the clock and note the exact time with seconds.

Aim to look at the clock again exactly when your Time Goal has elapsed.

Five minutes is the Level 1 Time Goal, so start here on your first Time Awareness Training.

If you've done Time Awareness Training before, start at the last Time Goal you've earned.

When you think your Time Goal has elapsed, look at the clock.

You may only look at the clock once per Time Awareness Training.

If you look at the clock within one minute of your Time Goal, progress your Time Goal to the next Level tomorrow.

To progress to the next level of Time Awareness Training, you must check the clock within only one minute of your Time Goal.

If you've checked the time within one minute of the Level 5 Time Goal, congratulations! You've graduated from Time Awareness Training.

If you look at the clock farther than one minute from your Time Goal, this round of Time Awareness Training is now over.

Please restart Time Awareness Training with the same Time Goal tomorrow.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill (35 Version)
sequence.text:
2
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill (35 Version)
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

Read, translate, and quip every sentence*. Max every two sentences if they are really simple. Exactly how you would translate in LR. 

At the end of each paragraph, pause to review the Translation while looking at the paragraph and confirm with yourself that you really know it. 

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

After each paragraph, relook at all the paragraphs that you've read so far to confirm they are placed in your memory. 

Continue on until the end of the passage with the same process.

At the end of the passage, do a final review by relooking at the entire passage and reconfirming your Translation. This should take about 30 seconds.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Pacing Practice
sequence.text:
3
Pacing Practice
Instructions

Choose an interval time goal.

Your interval time goal is your target time for each question.

For example, an interval time goal may be 90 seconds per question.

Follow the procedures of How to Set a Realistic Interval Time Goal below.

Set an interval timer to repeatedly countdown from that time goal 30 times in a row.

Do not incorporate rest intervals.

We choose 30 times so we can have some extra intervals in case our timer messes up.

Start your interval timer when you begin an LR or RC section*.

For RC, only use the interval timer on the questions, not during the passage.

You must select an answer on each question before the interval timer goes off.

You cannot stay on a question longer than the interval timer permits, no matter how badly you want to.
SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Stop Mental and Physical Self-Sabotage

What problem are we solving?

Have you ever done a section when:

  • you're falling asleep in the middle? 

  • someone else is taking a call a little too close to you? 

  • you're looking at the clock over and over again and saying to yourself "I have to speed up"?

  • you're saying to yourself, "I can't get this wrong. Oh my god, I don't understand. I have to get it. I'll never get into Berkeley. My dad is right about me."?

  • you just saw a previous score and you're going to cry?

  • you have a stye on your left eye and also maybe COVID?

Doing the LSAT like this is mental and physical self-sabotage.

You are willfully engaging in behaviors that decrease your score. 

I care about you and I care about your score, so I'm going to give you some real talk here.

Telling yourself you can't do something drastically increases the chances you won't be able to do that thing.

So stop it. 

Doing LSAT in an environment or situation that pulls on your attention sets you up to fail.

So stop it.

Thinking about the past, the future, and what other people think while you're doing the LSAT ensures that you do not do your best.

So stop it.

This is your Olympics.

We need you in peak mental and physical condition while you're training to ensure that you're in peak condition on test day. This means that you have to advocate for yourself.

Create space in your life for LSAT is to be the #1 priority, not something you do after every high priority is done.

This Accuracy Fix teaches you how to be that your advocate.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Decaf RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

We're a little less scared of RC now, so we can move our Decaf to a warmup and let you choose what Translation style you want to use on your Light Inside Out. 

If you want to stick with Decaf, that's fine, but feel free to move to Cappuccino or Caffeinated if that's more comfortable for you. 

Light Inside Out is a little less work than Modified Inside Out, so you should still feel comfortable with RC without as much energy expenditure. It still spoils the passage, so there's no worries there. 

We add some Tone Training to get you used to feeling the author's emotions through the passage. That way you won't be as intimidated when you have to do Tone questions in a timed environment.

How This Should Be Done

This is another Routine where I really don't want you to rush.

This Routine might take a little less time than the Make RC Easy Routine, but slow and steady wins the race, especially if you're changing the RC Translation Drill away from Decaf.

Remember the point of the I'm Afraid of RC Routine Progression is to fix your RC mindset. If the Routine isn't helping your mindset, it's not doing its job.

How to Move On

If you feel less fear (but still a little bit of fear) toward RC, move on to the Learn to Love RC Routine, the next Routine in the I'm Afraid of RC Routine Progression.

If you don't feel any fear toward RC, move on to any of the I Just Want to Focus on RC Routine Progressions.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Decaf RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

sequence.name: RC Thunderdome
sequence.text:
2
RC Thunderdome
Instructions

For each passage*, write out an answer to each of the following:

What's the Main Point?

What's the tone of the passage?

Who is the author?

Who is the audience?

Who are the players in the passage and what do they believe?

Strengthen the author's opinion

If the passage feels neutral, write a confirming piece of evidence for the information the author is presenting.

Weaken the author's opinion

If the passage feels neutral, write a disconfirming piece of evidence for the information the author is presenting.

Three Inferences from the passage

Three things the author is likely to believe

Parallel one piece of the passage

Pick an example, one line of reasoning, or a given person's point of view.

Outline the structure of the passage

You can use paragraphs as an organizing structure, but you can also delineate on a more fine-grained level, if desired.

Sub out three words in the passage and replace them with a new word/phrase that means the same thing.

Pick three sentences out of the passage and identify their function

Identify a principle underlying the passage as a whole or an argument within the passage

3
Write In
Instructions

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*. 

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

Write in a correct answer to the question.

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine exists to force students to refine their autonomous thinking when it comes to RC answer choices.

If you're overly reliant on the answer choices to suggest at you, you'll always be at their mercy. 

The RC Thunderdome multiplies every passage into almost every question type and doesn't give you any answer choices to suggest any correct outcomes. This is a great Routine for finding out where you have trouble thinking for yourself and then reviewing accordingly. 

But then, by moving directly into an RC Write In, we get to take our Thunderdome skills and actualize them into a real question-answering section immediately.

The RC Write In forces you to actually make a Mission on RC, but having just done an RC Thunderdome, you'll be more than prepared to do so.

How This Should Be Done

You can customize how long you spend on the RC Thunderdome before going into the RC Write In.

Ideally, you'll have time to do a full section of Thunderdoming. But given that Thunderdoming can take a fair amount of time, especially when you haven't done many before, you might want to cap your Thunderdome at one or two passages and then move directly into your Write In.

For the Write In, use natural pace timing, but keep adrenaline in your veins.

How to Move On

When your Write Ins directly overlap with the correct answer more often than not and you don't have any remaining hesitation with any of your RC Thunderdome outputs, you can progress to a new Advanced Routine. (Perhaps integrating an RC HIIT into the mix?)

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Don't Be Desperate in the Answers
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Don't Be Desperate in the Answers

What problem are we solving?

Sometimes you just want to get the question right so badly that every answer choice looks like an escape hatch.

"Is it right? Is it right!??

If it's right, then I can move on.

Then I won't waste any more time.

Then the stimulus must have meant this.

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Masterpiece
sequence.text:
2
Masterpiece
Instructions

NOTE: Masterpieces are multi-day workouts focused on a single section*. You can do a three-day Masterpiece or a four-day Masterpiece to start. Don't worry, you do less and less work as the Masterpiece progresses each day.

Complete the section in any workout style.

Mark questions for hyperskip, but don't perform your hyperskip pass yet.

When you're done with the section, put it aside without grading it.

The next day, redo each question in the section fully.

When you return to the section, keep your answer selected at first, but uncross off all other answer choices.

Do not just look at your previous answer without actually redoing the full question. Your objective is to decide whether you want to stick to your previous answer or choose a new answer.

On each question you have three options:

Lock in your previous answer.

Once an answer is locked, you will not look at this question again until Camo Day. Locking is a way to signal to yourself that you know this answer is correct and do not need to look at it again.

Do not lock in more than 50% of your remaining answers on any lock-in pass until you get to the last day of your Masterpiece.

Keep your answer the same, but leave the question unlocked.

Leave a question unlocked if you are not sure about whether the answer you've selected is correct.

Change your answer.

If you change your answer, you may not lock the question on this pass.

The next day, return only to your unlocked questions and redo them. Decide to lock in or change your answers, following the same procedure you did on day 2.

This process repeats for however many days your Masterpiece will last.

Make sure all questions are locked in by the last day.

Optional: On the last day, print out a fresh copy of the section and redo it straight-through.

Compare the fresh section to your locked-in answers and see if there are any differences. If so, reconcile the two sections. Decide on your final answer before putting it into Camo.

After your last pass on the section, with all answers locked in, proceed with Camo and Wrong Answer Journaling.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

    2. When you're done with the section, put it aside without grading it.

  2. The next day, redo each question in the section fully.

    1. When you return to the section, keep your answer selected at first, but uncross off all other answer choices.

    2. Do not just look at your previous answer without actually redoing the full question. Your objective is to decide whether you want to stick to your previous answer or choose a new answer.

    3. On each question you have three options:

      1. Lock in your previous answer.

        1. Once an answer is locked, you will not look at this question again until Camo Day. Locking is a way to signal to yourself that you know this answer is correct and do not need to look at it again.

        2. Do not lock in more than 50% of your remaining answers on any lock-in pass until you get to the last day of your Masterpiece.

      2. Keep your answer the same, but leave the question unlocked.

        1. Leave a question unlocked if you are not sure about whether the answer you've selected is correct.

      3. Change your answer.

        1. If you change your answer, you may not lock the question on this pass.

  3. The next day, return only to your unlocked questions and redo them. Decide to lock in or change your answers, following the same procedure you did on day 2.

    1. This process repeats for however many days your Masterpiece will last.

    2. Make sure all questions are locked in by the last day.

  4. Optional: On the last day, print out a fresh copy of the section and redo it straight-through.

    1. Compare the fresh section to your locked-in answers and see if there are any differences. If so, reconcile the two sections. Decide on your final answer before putting it into Camo.

  5. After your last pass on the section, with all answers locked in, proceed with Camo and Wrong Answer Journaling.

Why Are We Doing This?

There's a real-recognize-real quality to some students and the RC Masterpiece. Sometimes you just know that the RC Masterpiece's impulse control techniques were made for you (because they were ❤️‍🩹).

If nothing seems to improve your score, this Routine is for you.

How This Should Be Done

Since the RC Masterpiece takes different amounts of time on different days, you can contract or extend the Extracurricular Reading and Vocab Training time to fill your homework block.

For example, if you're on the third day of your RC Masterpiece and you don't actually have that many questions to complete, use that time as an opportunity to dive more deeply into your Extracurricular Reading and Vocab Training.

You can also layer this Routine with second RC Masterpiece section on a staggered start day. This means you would begin another RC Masterpiece section on day 2 or 3 of another section's RC Masterpiece. This would allow you to get more RC Masterpiece sections done throughout the week and potentially see a lot more improvement.

How to Move On

Move on from this Routine when your accuracy improves.

RC Masterpieces are great as temporary but intense Routines, but you don't need to stay on RC Masterpieces any longer than is necessary to move the accuracy.

sequence.name: Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Cappuccino RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Cappuccino is similar to Decaf, except instead of recapping all of your Translations after finishing with each paragraph, you’ll be looking back at the text to confirm your Translations.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with the paragraph you just read.

In this step, you are not rereading from scratch. 

You're confirming the Translation you already have is right. 

This style of confirming your Translation with the text applies to every confirmation you ever do on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Take a few seconds to confirm your Translation with all the text you've read of the passage so far.

This confirmation step will include all the paragraphs you've read so far.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

OPTIONAL: Look away and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of the entire passage silently.

This step is optional, but you should do it when you first begin Cappuccino RC Translation Drills and periodically afterward, just to confirm that you can.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Intuition, Not Impulse
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Intuition, Not Impulse

What problem are we solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

inline_prep.text:
Accuracy
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
Prep Map
/
Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
What Problem Are We Solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
1
Decaf RC Translation Drill
1 PASSAGE
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine addresses the memory-blanking issue that afflicts many students when attempting to complete a passage's questions.

If you find yourself getting deep into the questions, but forgetting large aspects of the passage even though you've properly translated it, this Routine will fix that memory issue.

It's really an under-reported story how much of excellence on the LSAT comes down to working memory capacity and it's sad that most people think they can't improve their working memory.

I know that you can improve your working memory, and I know that this Routine will help you do so. Don't give up even though it might be hard sometimes. You're getting better and it matters.

How This Should Be Done

You can approach this Routine while you're still attempting to beat MemAC Level 5, or as a refresher after you've beaten MemAC Level 5. It'll work out your working memory either way. 

You can customize the amount of MemAC to make the length of this Routine work for you. You can do up to a full section of MemAC, as little as 10 questions of MemAC, or you cap MemAC at 30/60 minutes. More MemAC is more effective, but do what you can.

How to Move On

When you're remembering all the details on your Passage Rebound and it is no longer challenging, you can move on to another Accuracy Fix Routine.

Accuracy
Strengthen Your Working Memory
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Strengthen Your Working Memory

What problem are we solving?

You know that feeling when your memory just goes blank in the middle of a question? And you kinda have no idea what you're supposed to do?

Yeah, that's not supposed to happen.

That's something to train out of you.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine is a safe place to get your rebellious instincts out.

It shows you how good you are and also how the process affects your sections. For the right test taker, it can be a great way to get night-before-the-test jitters out.

Recently, one of my tutoring students did this Routine the night before his test and he got a 177 the next day.

Correlation or causation? You be the judge 😂

Often, the scores on DARE Sections and Anti-PTs don't go down nearly as much as the student thinks they will.

Other times, the scores will reduce significantly and it reminds students why they do the process in the first place. No matter what, it's surprisingly comforting.

How This Should Be Done

This is the Routine where you purposefully break all of my rules.

Enjoy living free. I don't want to give you too much advice on how this should be done because the whole point is to screw around. 

But on the DARE Section, make sure that you feel the pain of not being sure, but having to choose an early answer anyway.

This an exaggerated experience to show you how risky it is to choose an answer without reading them all.

How to Move On

This Routine is something you'll only do one or two times maximum.

There's no real need to move on from it since it's kind of a one-off anyway.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits

What problem are we solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... What Problem Are We Solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

sequence.name: Density Buckets
sequence.text:
2
Density Buckets
Instructions

Make a spreadsheet with two columns, or use this template:

Column 1: High Density

Column 2: Low Density

Complete an LR section* using any workout, but with one small adjustment: Write your Mission in either the High-Density or Low-Density column in the spreadsheet.

Choose which column to place your Mission into based on how information-dense your Mission is.

The High Density column is where you write your high information density Missions.

A Mission with high information density will use words and concepts from the stimulus directly without referential phrasing, glazing over the details, and characterizing information ("all that stuff") to avoid having to say it directly.

Example Mission in the High-Density Bucket: Whether there actually is more food in the ocean tropics versus the freshwater tropics

The Low Density column is where you write your low information density Missions.

A Mission with low information density will use referential phrasing ("this," "that," "it," "they," "the conclusion," etc.) to gloss over the direct words and concepts from the stimulus, omit the details like specific nouns and verbs, and group information together with broad characterizations ("good things").

Example Mission on the Same Question in the Low-Density Bucket: Food is important

After you complete the section, review the spreadsheet to note which questions produced Low-Density Missions.

Return to the questions that produced Low-Density Missions the next day and try to make a new higher density Mission before you Camo the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS
Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Density Buckets and the Method Vocab Remix hold you accountable to using the complex language of LR in context.

If you notice that your internal monologue is vague and you tend to make remarks like "all these answers sound the same," this is the Routine for you.

This Routine gives you the verbal tools to raise your score, and gives you the chance to put those tools into action.

Make sure you know the Uncut Method Vocab List before you take on this Routine. The Method Vocab Remix will get you to start using this vocab in your own internal monologue. Once it's in your brain, you'll be able to master LR on a whole new level.

How This Should Be Done

Take your time with the Method Vocab Remix to really make your answer choices sound like actual LSAT answer choices. It's not worth rushing it and not really learning how to use the words. 

Don't be afraid to throw your Mission in the Low Density Column during your Density Buckets. It's so much better to be for real with yourself rather than pretending something is high density information when you know it's not. This is how you'll improve.

How to Move On

When two Missions or fewer are in the Low Density column on your Density Buckets and you've completed the Method Vocab Remix, you're safe to move on from this Routine. You can progress to any other Accuracy Fix Routine.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits

What problem are we solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
What Problem Are We Solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

Stop Oversimplifying
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Stop Oversimplifying

What problem are we solving?

There is no such thing as "just a detail" on the LSAT. 

Ignoring "details" leads to missing question through oversimplifying. If you run with an inaccurate, oversimplified version of the text, you're bound to miss questions.

Answers are right and wrong based on "just one word." That doesn't make the LSAT mean, evil, or unfair. It makes the LSAT a test of precision.

And precision is something you'd to have when you're a lawyer, right? You don't want to be the attorney who harms their client because you missed "just one word." 

Every word on the LSAT deserves equal levels of respect, as it works with every other word to create a conceptual Translation of each sentence.

Conceptual Translation can be the single biggest differentiator between high and lower scorers. It is the opposite of oversimplifying. When you ignore some words in an answer choice and focus solely on other words (keywording), you're not conceptually translating that answer. You're oversimplifying and massively increasing your risk of missing the question.

Keywording reduces an answer's fate solely to whether it has certain words from the stimulus.

However, there are many correct answers that contain no words from the stimulus. There are many wrong answers that contain tons of words from the stimulus. 

You cannot oversimplify answer choice selection to a shallow matching game and expect the LSAT to tolerate it. It won't. 

But this is just one way oversimplification decreases your score. There are approximately one million other ways oversimplification decreases your score. 

This Accuracy Fix trains you to embrace complexity because your mind is strong enough to handle it. Luckily, this is something you were trained to do in the Translation Prep Stage. Now is the time to put that training into action, especially in the answer choices. 

That's how we stop you from missing so many questions.

inline_prep.name: Stop Oversimplifying
inline_prep.text:
Accuracy
FIX 2 OF 7
Stop Oversimplifying
Prep Map
/
Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 2 OF 7
Stop Oversimplifying
What Problem Are We Solving?

There is no such thing as "just a detail" on the LSAT. 

Ignoring "details" leads to missing question through oversimplifying. If you run with an inaccurate, oversimplified version of the text, you're bound to miss questions.

Answers are right and wrong based on "just one word." That doesn't make the LSAT mean, evil, or unfair. It makes the LSAT a test of precision.

And precision is something you'd to have when you're a lawyer, right? You don't want to be the attorney who harms their client because you missed "just one word." 

Every word on the LSAT deserves equal levels of respect, as it works with every other word to create a conceptual Translation of each sentence.

Conceptual Translation can be the single biggest differentiator between high and lower scorers. It is the opposite of oversimplifying. When you ignore some words in an answer choice and focus solely on other words (keywording), you're not conceptually translating that answer. You're oversimplifying and massively increasing your risk of missing the question.

Keywording reduces an answer's fate solely to whether it has certain words from the stimulus.

However, there are many correct answers that contain no words from the stimulus. There are many wrong answers that contain tons of words from the stimulus. 

You cannot oversimplify answer choice selection to a shallow matching game and expect the LSAT to tolerate it. It won't. 

But this is just one way oversimplification decreases your score. There are approximately one million other ways oversimplification decreases your score. 

This Accuracy Fix trains you to embrace complexity because your mind is strong enough to handle it. Luckily, this is something you were trained to do in the Translation Prep Stage. Now is the time to put that training into action, especially in the answer choices. 

That's how we stop you from missing so many questions.

How You Know You Need To Do This

sequence.name: The Island
sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

Click here to go to The Island (scroll to the bottom!)

sequence.name: Timing Failsafe
sequence.text:
3
Timing Failsafe
Instructions

NOTE: You can do a Timing Failsafe with any Workout. Failsafes are time-training protocols that you can apply to any Workout.

Set your accuracy goal as a target number of wrong answers per section.

An accuracy goal could be -5, for example.

Timing Rules

First Day: Do a stopwatch-timed section* to establish your baseline natural pace.

All Other Days: Adopt the timing pattern that you earned by beating or not beating the Failsafe the previous study day. Use a countdown timer for section timing once you have begun to lower your time goal.

Complete an LR or RC section.

Take a five-minute break and Camo the section you just completed.

If you have met your accuracy goal, proceed to a second section of the same type with the same timing pattern.

This means if you just completed an RC section in 42 minutes and you hit your accuracy goal of -5, you would proceed to do another RC section in 42 minutes with an accuracy goal of -5.

If you have not met your accuracy goal on the first section, you have not beaten today's Failsafe.

Don't lower your time goal tomorrow.

Do not proceed to a second section of the same type today.

Instead, Wrong Answer Journal and do one Recovery Workouts (listed below) now.

If you have proceeded to a second section, take a five-minute break and Camo it.

If have met your accuracy goal for the second time in a row, you have beaten today's Failsafe!

Lower your time goal tomorrow.

Wrong Answer Journal both of today's sections.

If you do not meet the accuracy goal on the second section, you have not beaten today's Failsafe.

Do not move the time the next day.

Wrong Answer Journal both of today's sections.

Return to Step 1 the following day.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

  1. After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

  2. For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

    1. This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

  3. Fill in your Reason Missed column

    1. In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

      1. Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

    2. The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

      1. Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

      2. This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

  4. Fill in your Solution column

    1. In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

      1. Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

    2. The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

      1. Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

    3. Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Timing Failsafe Routines are one of the only ways to effectively reduce time without Marathoning.

The upsides of Timing Failsafes are:

They can be done in shorter periods of time than a Marathon

They allow for more systematic gradual time reduction

Review can be more targeted and frequent

This Routine works great for students who thrive on structure.

How This Should Be Done

Failsafe Routines work best when combined with other Routines to bring time down while maintaining accuracy.

Essentially, you have to address the reasons why the Failsafe breaks in order to get it to progress, so you'll want to consider alternating Failsafe Routines with the Accuracy Fix Routines that pertain to your mistakes.

How to Move On

Timing Failsafe Routines can get you to test-day goal time and accuracy without progressing to any other Speed Routine.

However, if you have lost every Timing Failsafe you've attempted for three consecutive prep days, here are a few options for what you can try next:

If you're hitting your goal time and accuracy in the majority of your sections, take a Practice Test (PT).

You can move to any of the other Speed Routines, if your Timing Failsafe Routine went well. You do not have to go in order.
