sequence.name: The Island
sequence.text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

sequence.name: Timing Failsafe
sequence.text:
3
Timing Failsafe
Instructions

NOTE: You can do a Timing Failsafe with any Workout. Failsafes are time-training protocols that you can apply to any Workout.

Set your accuracy goal as a target number of wrong answers per section.

An accuracy goal could be -5, for example.

Timing Rules

First Day: Do a stopwatch-timed section* to establish your baseline natural pace.

All Other Days: Adopt the timing pattern that you earned by beating or not beating the Failsafe the previous study day. Use a countdown timer for section timing once you have begun to lower your time goal.

Complete an LR or RC section.

Take a five-minute break and Camo the section you just completed.

If you have met your accuracy goal, proceed to a second section of the same type with the same timing pattern.

This means if you just completed an RC section in 42 minutes and you hit your accuracy goal of -5, you would proceed to do another RC section in 42 minutes with an accuracy goal of -5.

If you have not met your accuracy goal on the first section, you have not beaten today's Failsafe.

Don't lower your time goal tomorrow.

Do not proceed to a second section of the same type today.

Instead, Wrong Answer Journal and do one Recovery Workouts (listed below) now.

If you have proceeded to a second section, take a five-minute break and Camo it.

If have met your accuracy goal for the second time in a row, you have beaten today's Failsafe!

Lower your time goal tomorrow.

Wrong Answer Journal both of today's sections.

If you do not meet the accuracy goal on the second section, you have not beaten today's Failsafe.

Do not move the time the next day.

Wrong Answer Journal both of today's sections.

Return to Step 1 the following day.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Decaf RC Translation Drill
sequence.text:
2
Decaf RC Translation Drill
≥ 1 SECTION
Instructions

NOTE: Do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1*. Do it just like LR.

This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.

Quip after every Translation. 

This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.

Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 1 silently.

The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.

The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

    2. The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.

    3. The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.

    4. It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.

    5. This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.

  3. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.

  4. Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 2 silently.

  5. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.

  6. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.

  7. Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the FULL TRANSLATION of paragraph 3 silently.

  8. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.

  9. Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

  10. Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

4
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Decaf is one of the most intense, difficult Workouts on the whole Prep Map. It's also magical.

By the end of Decaf, you can actually say the whole Translation of the passage out loud from memory. Doesn't that sound like a goal worth sweating for?

How This Should Be Done

Adding Decaf RC Translation to your Routine means you'll have less time for your Translation + CLIR Drills. This should be fine because your Translation + CLIR Drills are taking less time than they used to, so you should ideally be able to maintain the same Translation + CLIR Drill volume as you did in the Intro Translation Routine (Translation Routine 1).

Make sure to watch the Decaf video explanation and demo before trying Decaf on your own (all linked below). It really helps to see me do it before you try it yourself.

Your progression toward the Decaf RC Translation time and accuracy goals is primarily determined by two things: volume and following the instructions. Do at least 1 full section of Decaf RC Translation per day, if possible. Ideally, you would complete 3 consecutive sections of Decaf RC Translation per day.

If you don't practice Decaf every day or don't follow the Decaf instructions, it will stay difficult longer. To maximize your progress in this Routine, only do Decaf Translation Drills on whole sections at a time. Do not split up Decaf Translation Drills into individual passages or take breaks between passages. The number one way to improve quickly at Decaf RC Translation is volume, and if you only do one passage per day the volume will be too low to allow for progress.

Do not compromise the Translation and recap standard outlined in the Decaf RC Translation instructions. If you do not recap with all the details or do not quip, you are not completing Decaf RC Translation and should not progress to the next Routine.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Once you hit the Translation + CLIR time goal, ideally while maintaining accuracy of -5 or better against the CLIR Answer Key, you can move on to the AC Primer + Decaf Routine.

We move to the Answer Choice Primer next so we can bring your newfound Translation skills into the answer choices.

Translation + CLIR Goals

The time goal for Translation + CLIR Drills is 20 minutes.

The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations.

Meeting this Translation + CLIR Drill time goal is only valid under two conditions:

You have a CLIR for every stimulus.

You have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section out loud.

How to Pull This Off

Adding Decaf RC Translation to your Routine means you'll have less time for your Translation + CLIR Drills. This should be fine because your Translation + CLIR Drills are taking less time than they used to, so you should ideally be able to maintain the same Translation + CLIR Drill volume as you did in the Intro Translation Routine (Translation Routine 1).

Make sure to watch the Decaf video explanation and demo before trying Decaf on your own (all linked below). It really helps to see me do it before you try it yourself.

Your progression toward the Decaf RC Translation time and accuracy goals is primarily determined by two things: volume and following the instructions. Do at least 1 full section of Decaf RC Translation per day, if possible. Ideally, you would complete 3 consecutive sections of Decaf RC Translation per day.

If you don't practice Decaf every day or don't follow the Decaf instructions, it will stay difficult longer. To maximize your progress in this Routine, only do Decaf Translation Drills on whole sections at a time. Do not split up Decaf Translation Drills into individual passages or take breaks between passages. The number one way to improve quickly at Decaf RC Translation is volume, and if you only do one passage per day the volume will be too low to allow for progress.

Do not compromise the Translation and recap standard outlined in the Decaf RC Translation instructions. If you do not recap with all the details or do not quip, you are not completing Decaf RC Translation and should not progress to the next Routine.

How to move on

Once you hit the Translation + CLIR time goal, ideally while maintaining accuracy of -5 or better against the CLIR Answer Key, you can move on to the AC Primer + Decaf Routine.

We move to the Answer Choice Primer next so we can bring your newfound Translation skills into the answer choices.

  • The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations.

  • Meeting this Translation + CLIR Drill time goal is only valid under two conditions:

    • You have a CLIR for every stimulus.

    • You have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section out loud.

Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

The Translation + CLIR Drills in this Routine are the foundation of your entire LSAT prep journey. This is the most important homework you will do during your LSAT prep training, even compared to PTs.

This Routine builds a foundation in LR Translation before we port your Translation skills over to RC in the next Routine.

How This Should Be Done

Your progression toward the Translation time and accuracy goals is primarily determined by two things: volume and following the instructions.

To maximize your progress in this Routine, do all your Translation + CLIR Drills consecutively; do not take breaks between Translation + CLIR Drills. Do not review your Translation + CLIR Drills in between sections. All review should be done in a separate sitting.

Do at least 3 consecutive Translation + CLIR Drills per day, if possible. Ideally, you would complete 6 Translation + CLIR drills consecutively per day. Doing 1 Translation + CLIR Drill per day will not improve your skills; it will keep your skills the same. You will only start improving on your second consecutive Translation + CLIR Drill; this is why it is so useful to do at least 3 consecutive Translation + CLIR Drills every day.

Add a Translation Marathon to your Daily Practice at least once per week. If you can manage to do Translation + CLIR Marathons more often, you will progress to the time goal faster.

Extracurricular Reading and Vocab should always be done at the end of your Routine to gradually expand your common sense in the subject areas where you're weakest. If you struggle with science passages, emphasize daily science engagement in the Extracurricular Reading. If you struggle with abstract language, emphasize daily humanities engagement in the Extracurricular Reading.

SHOW LESS
How to Move On

Once you are halfway to your Translation + CLIR Drill time goal, move to the next Routine: Translation + Decaf.

The time goal for Translation + CLIR Drills is 20 minutes. The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations. sequence.name: Translation + CLIR Drill
sequence.text:
1
Translation + CLIR Drill
≥ 3 SECTIONS
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

sequence.name: Extracurricular Reading
sequence.text:
2
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
3
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Foundation Translation Routine

Why are we doing this?

The Translation + CLIR Drills in this Routine are the foundation of your entire LSAT prep journey. This is the most important homework you will do during your LSAT prep training, even compared to PTs.

This Routine builds a foundation in LR Translation before we port your Translation skills over to RC in the next Routine.

LR
RC

Challenge IndexPretty Chill
LevelBeginner

Time goal to move on20 min

Routine Schedule

Do these workouts in this order. For real, the order matters.

1

Translation + CLIR Drill

≥ 3 sections
2

Extracurricular Reading

3

Vocab Training

Once A Week, Do This Instead

1

8 sections
≥ 1x per week

How to Pull This Off

Your progression toward the Translation time and accuracy goals is primarily determined by two things: volume and following the instructions.

To maximize your progress in this Routine, do all your Translation + CLIR Drills consecutively; do not take breaks between Translation + CLIR Drills. Do not review your Translation + CLIR Drills in between sections. All review should be done in a separate sitting.

Do at least 3 consecutive Translation + CLIR Drills per day, if possible. Ideally, you would complete 6 Translation + CLIR drills consecutively per day. Doing 1 Translation + CLIR Drill per day will not improve your skills; it will keep your skills the same. You will only start improving on your second consecutive Translation + CLIR Drill; this is why it is so useful to do at least 3 consecutive Translation + CLIR Drills every day.

Add a Translation Marathon to your Daily Practice at least once per week. If you can manage to do Translation + CLIR Marathons more often, you will progress to the time goal faster.

Extracurricular Reading and Vocab should always be done at the end of your Routine to gradually expand your common sense in the subject areas where you're weakest. If you struggle with science passages, emphasize daily science engagement in the Extracurricular Reading. If you struggle with abstract language, emphasize daily humanities engagement in the Extracurricular Reading.

How to move on

Once you are halfway to your Translation + CLIR Drill time goal, move to the next Routine: Translation + Decaf.

The time goal for Translation + CLIR Drills is 20 minutes. The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations. Meeting this Translation + CLIR Drill time goal is only valid under two conditions: you have a CLIR for every stimulus and you have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section out loud. Ideally, you should hit -5 accuracy against the CLIR Answer Key consistently in order to beat the time goal, but this accuracy goal may be adjusted according to your score goals.

Example of When to Move On: You started at 52 minutes per out loud Translation + CLIR Drill section and you don't have accommodations, so your time goal is 20 minutes. The midpoint of 52 and 20 is 36, so you would move on when your time hits 36 minutes.

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
1
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
2
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

I love putting Camo + Wrong Answer Journaling in its own block once per week!

Whenever a student is flexible enough in tutoring to allow this Routine to be added to their schedule (instead of daily Camoing), I always take advantage of it because this Routine enables so much more insight from the review.

When students Camo daily, they will often rush it just to see the score, decline to Wrong Answer Journal, and move Camo to the first task in the Routine. Emotional reactions to the results then distract the student from the sections they're about to do, and performance is compromised.

I want all of your sections to represent your absolute best, which is why I want you to do this Camo Day Routine instead of the compromised daily Camoing described above.

How This Should Be Done

Do this Routine once per week. There are a ton of specific instructions on exactly how to Camo and exactly how to Wrong Answer Journal in each Workout's instructions.

Please read the Camo Review and Wrong Answer Journal instructions in detail and follow what is written there.

How to Move On

You never move on from Camo and Wrong Answer Journaling 🏆

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Learn From Your Mistakes
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Learn From Your Mistakes

What problem are we solving?

Seeing the score is like popping a balloon. 

You want to see the score so bad. Because you need to "see how you're doing," "understand where you are," "stay motivated," and "know what to work on."

So, of course, you need to check the score as soon as you're done with the section.  But suddenly, as soon as you see that number.

There's nothing interesting left anymore. 

Now you "know where you are," but the emotional reaction to where you are overwhelms any hope of strategic insights. 

If you like the number, you'll walk away excited and think, "Okay, now I'm good."

And then the next section is likely to crash and burn from laziness and complacency. You don't need to work that hard when you're good, right? 

If you don't like the number, tears follow.

Now there's no motivation to continue because nothing ever works. So what's the point? Why try? I should just give up and save the effort I would waste on this. I never get better. 

When you do this, you actively decline to change the behaviors that caused your wrong answers. This causes you to not improve.

Failing to look inward to understand what you need to change will cause you to leave points on the table.

This Accuracy Fix stops that rollercoaster of pain and plateaus.

You can get better. Give yourself the chance to really understand what you're doing wrong.

FIX 3 OF 7
Learn From Your Mistakes
What Problem Are We Solving?

Seeing the score is like popping a balloon. 

You want to see the score so bad. Because you need to "see how you're doing," "understand where you are," "stay motivated," and "know what to work on."

So, of course, you need to check the score as soon as you're done with the section.  But suddenly, as soon as you see that number.

There's nothing interesting left anymore. 

Now you "know where you are," but the emotional reaction to where you are overwhelms any hope of strategic insights. 

If you like the number, you'll walk away excited and think, "Okay, now I'm good."

And then the next section is likely to crash and burn from laziness and complacency. You don't need to work that hard when you're good, right? 

If you don't like the number, tears follow.

Now there's no motivation to continue because nothing ever works. So what's the point? Why try? I should just give up and save the effort I would waste on this. I never get better. 

When you do this, you actively decline to change the behaviors that caused your wrong answers. This causes you to not improve.

Failing to look inward to understand what you need to change will cause you to leave points on the table.

This Accuracy Fix stops that rollercoaster of pain and plateaus.

You can get better. Give yourself the chance to really understand what you're doing wrong.

sequence.text:
2
RC Straight Through
Inside Out
1 SECTION
ALTERNATE
Instructions
RC Straight Through
Inside Out

Translate the passage*.

Proceed to the first question and translate the question stem.

Make a Mission.

Making a Mission means answering the question yourself.

Go back to the passage to enable yourself to answer the question, if needed. Only look back at the passage in the Mission stage of the question.

Don't try to match your Mission in the answer choices.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the standard of what the question stem is asking.

If you think this answer meets the standard of the question stem, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the standard of the question stem, leave it open.

If you know this answer does not meets the standard of the question stem, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip a total of 5-7 questions per section.

Only go back to your hyperskips at the end of the entire section, not at the end of the passage they're associated with.

You can go back to the passage during the hyperskip.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

Your goal in this Routine (and every Accuracy Routine) is to improve your score.

This first Accuracy Routine should help you diagnose which Accuracy Fixes are relevant to you and proceed to the Routines associated with each Accuracy Fix.

Remember, the reason your score is not already at your goal is because you are making bad decisions at various points throughout the section. The question type didn't choose the wrong answer. The difficulty level didn't choose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer.

When you look at your wrong answers throughout the Accuracy Prep Stage, only analyze them through the lens of what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer.

Once you isolate the cause of your bad decision-making, you can choose the appropriate Accuracy Fix and begin Routines designed to address the areas causing your wrong answers, which will improve your score.

How This Should Be Done

Change the order of your sections each day so you do LR first one day and RC first the next.

If you want to try to fit this Routine into a 2-hour study block, be sure you pair Inside Out with the Acronym and the Mini-Cycle with Straight Through RC.

Whenever I say to "alternate" workouts in a Routine, switch which Workout you do each day. For example, if the Routine says, "Alternate: X // Y (1:1)," that means that I should do X on day 1 and then switch to doing Y the next time I do the Routine. The (1:1) numbers signal how many times you should do each Workout before switching to other Workout.

How to Move On

If Inside Out consistently outscores Straight Through RC, slow down your Straight Through RC and inspect exactly what Inside Out is giving you that Straight Through isn't. Your goal is to port that Inside Out accuracy to Straight Through RC, unless you have 70-minute accommodations and can stick with Inside Out on test day. 

If Straight Through RC consistently outscores Inside Out, lean into Straight Through RC and omit the Inside Out from the Routine. 

If the Mini-Cycles consistently outscores the Acronym, slow down your Acronym and inspect exactly what the Mini-Cycle is forcing you to do that you are omitting in the Acronym. Check off every step of the Acronym on paper until you're confident you're committing to every single step of the process. 

If you see decreased accuracy on the Mini-Cycle, you likely have a stamina issue and can't maintain focus all the way through the Workout. If you're seeing better accuracy on the Acronym LR Section, lean into the Acronym and omit the Mini-Cycle from this Routine. 

Use your performance on this Routine to judge which Accuracy Fixes are relevant to you. Allow those Accuracy Fixes to direct which Workouts and Routines you practice next.

sequence.name: RC Straight Through
sequence.text:
2
RC Straight Through
Inside Out
1 SECTION
ALTERNATE
Instructions
RC Straight Through
Inside Out

Translate the passage*.

Proceed to the first question and translate the question stem.

Make a Mission.

Making a Mission means answering the question yourself.

Go back to the passage to enable yourself to answer the question, if needed. Only look back at the passage in the Mission stage of the question.

Don't try to match your Mission in the answer choices.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the standard of what the question stem is asking.

If you think this answer meets the standard of the question stem, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the standard of the question stem, leave it open.

If you know this answer does not meets the standard of the question stem, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip a total of 5-7 questions per section.

Only go back to your hyperskips at the end of the entire section, not at the end of the passage they're associated with.

You can go back to the passage during the hyperskip.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.text:
4
Extracurricular Reading
Instructions

Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:

ScienceDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC

Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting

Aeon.co

The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet

Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.

ALDaily.com

Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.

Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.

NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge

The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge

Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.

LSAT Relevant Guide Sections: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology

Crash Course

Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include

Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.

Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

sequence.name: Vocab Training
sequence.text:
5
Vocab Training
Instructions

Highlight any word you wouldn't bet your LSAT score on during all LSAT sections and during all Extracurricular Reading.

These highlighted words are your vocab words.

Harvest all the vocab words you've highlighted after your section or reading is complete.

Harvesting your words means writing down each of your vocab words in a tracker. You can use my template or create a simple Google Sheet for this.

Always harvest your vocab words the same day that you highlight them.

To further optimize your vocab harvesting, watch the How to Harvest Vocab Words video.

Practice your vocab words daily for at least 10 minutes.

To practice, follow the procedures outlined in the How to Learn Vocab Without AI video or the How to Learn Vocab: AI Supercharged Edition video.

10 minutes of practice is a minimum, not a maximum. If you have a 100+ number of vocab words to learn, do not be afraid to practice for a longer period of time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

Accuracy
Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits

What problem are we solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

Disrupt Your Toxic Habits
What Problem Are We Solving?

It's so easy to attribute a score you don't like to anything but your toxic habits. To say, "This one was just hard" or "I always have trouble with that question type." But none of those factors chose the wrong answer. You chose the wrong answer. And if you want your score to change, you have to change the toxic habits that made you choose that answer.

Toxic habits are like lifting weights with bad form – they feel like they're making lifting easier. But It's only a matter of time until you get injured. If you have bad form, you can't up your weight safely. Instead, you have to lower the weight and fix your form. (I would know... I had to have surgery to fix two hernias from bad weight-lighting form.)

The sad thing is that many toxic habits are recommended to well-meaning students who simply don't know any better. Just like the trainer who told me it was totally fine to up my weight way too fast.

If an "expert" tells you that you that only have to read the first word of most RC answers, who are you to know that's toxic? 

You just started LSAT prep. You don't know any better. And you accidentally adopt a toxic habit that lowers your score.

That is the information asymmetry that keeps me grinding beyond the point of rationality. I hate that information asymmetry because it lets people take advantage of you.

Advice like that decreases your score and you have to feel the pain of score variation to figure out that it was toxic in the first place.

That's why I've created and tested a non-toxic, proven LSAT process for the past 30,000+ hours. The processes in Loophole Online are built to replace toxic habits from the ground up.

Implementing non-toxic habits will get you the answer 100 out of 100 times when you implement it as instructed. That's what this Accuracy Fix trains you to do.

Intuition, Not Impulse
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Intuition, Not Impulse

What problem are we solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

inline_prep.text:
Accuracy
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
Prep Map
/
Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
What Problem Are We Solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

sequence.name: Write In
sequence.text:
2
Write In
Instructions

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*. 

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

Write in a correct answer to the question.

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Camo Review
sequence.text:
4
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

sequence.name: Wrong Answer Journal
sequence.text:
5
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

Ellen's Advice
Why Are We Doing This?

This Routine is an alternate Welcome to Accuracy Routine for those who feel like they want to throw up when they think about Party Tricking.

However, this Routine has its own unique benefits too beyond the fact that it doesn't include any Party Tricking.

Starting with a Write In LR section allows us to hone our Mission skills immediately, which is a huge value-add. Write Ins force you to manually identify the question type and make a Mission rather than gisting through the question stem.

This immediately improves accuracy or gets you to confront the fact that you don't really understand what the question is asking, which is another benefit since it tells us where we need to focus our training.

Modified Inside Out allows us smoothly transition into RC. If RC intimidates you, this Routine is a great choice.

I haven't found a way to make RC more accessible than Modified Inside Out, but you can always sub Light Inside Out into this Routine to sample another attempt I've made to solve the RC intimidation problem.

How This Should Be Done

Don't try to match your Write In answer in the answer choices.

You're doing the Write In to force yourself to answer the question on your own and build analytical autonomy, not to play a cheap matching game in the answer choices.

Change the order of your sections each day so you do LR first one day and RC first the next.

Whenever I say to "alternate" workouts in a Routine, switch which Workout you do each day. For example, if the Routine says, "Alternate: X // Y (1:1)," that means that I should do X on day 1 and then switch to doing Y the next time I do the Routine. The (1:1) numbers signal how many times you should do each Workout before switching to other Workout.

How to Move On

If Modified Inside Out consistently outscores Straight Through RC, slow down your Straight Through RC and inspect exactly what Modified Inside Out is giving you that Straight Through isn't. Your goal is to port that Modified Inside Out accuracy to Straight Through RC, unless you have 70-minute accommodations and can stick with Modified Inside Out on test day. 

If Straight Through RC consistently outscores Modified Inside Out, lean into Straight Through RC and omit the Modified Inside Out from the Routine. 

Use your performance on this Routine to judge which Accuracy Fixes are relevant to you. Allow those Accuracy Fixes to direct which Workouts and Routines you practice next.

Write In
Instructions

NOTE: The Write In replaces the Mission step of the Full LR Process.

Read and translate the stimulus in chunks*. 

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue until the end of the stimulus.

Mark the conclusion.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Read the question stem, identify the question type and whether the question is Powerful-Provable.

Write in a correct answer to the question.

Make the Write In answer sound like a real answer choice, not a messy note.

On every individual answer choice:

Read, translate, and quip the answer choice.

Investigate whether this answer choice meets the question type's Back Up Plan.

If you think this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, highlight the first word of the answer.

If you are not sure whether this answer meets the Back-Up Plan question, leave it open.

If you know this answer doesn't meet the Back-Up Plan question, cross it out.

Choose amongst the open and highlighted answer choices.

Hyperskip, if needed.

Aim to hyperskip 5-7 questions per section.

Use any remaining time to return to your hyperskips.

Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

inline_prep.html:
Accuracy
Intuition, Not Impulse
  1. Prep Map/
  2. Accuracy

Intuition, Not Impulse

What problem are we solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

Accuracy
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
Prep Map
/
Accuracy
TELL ELLEN
FIX 1 OF 7
Intuition, Not Impulse
What Problem Are We Solving?

Impulse is great until you have no idea why you chose a wrong answer.

Acting on impulse is like the evil twin of acting on intuition. It happens when you try to be fast before you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level.

Intuition takes over after you've ingrained the process at a subconscious level. Intuition can be reliable and purposeful. 

Impulse can't. 

I know you think I don't understand: "Like come on, Ellen. Don't you know I have to do this in 35 minutes?" I get you.

This advice is coming from someone who could -0 Logical Reasoning sections in 27 minutes one month after meeting the LSAT for the first time.

It's not that I love to be slow or want you to be slow; I actually love speed. My Spotify history of Eminem's Rap God has the receipts (yes that song is so problematic it's also so fast and it just soothes my brain so much).

But I want you to be right more than I want you to be fast. If you're right, you can train to be fast. If you're fast and wrong, you'll have to slow down to train to be right.

No matter how quickly or intuitively I ever choose an answer, if you were to freeze time and say, "Hey Ellen, why'd you do that?" I'd be able to tell you.

Even if I'm not consciously thinking out all the words behind my decision, I could tell you why I'm doing it. If you can't say why you're doing something, it creates score variation, the hallmark of acting on impulse rather than purpose.

There will be a time when you'll approach the LSAT intuitively, but that intuition will be rooted in strategy. This Accuracy Fix is meant to ingrain that reliable, process-driven strategy that will mature into intuition.

You take care of the process, and the process will take care of the test.

How You Know You Need To Do This
